records.applicability_limits: A ten-year-old blog post whose most concrete detail sits in comment threads; the authors state they had not quantified the developer-workflow cost of flakiness. Quarantine presumes someone is funded to drain the quarantine queue, which a small team may not be.
records.counter_evidence: Quarantine hides real regressions: one Google team found that when a previously stable test turned flaky the cause was a production defect roughly one time in six, so removing it from the blocking path can suppress a genuine failure.

records.source: Jeff Listfield, Where do our flaky tests come from? (Google Testing Blog)
records.study_design: Observational analysis of historical test-result data
records.population: Approximately 4.2 million tests in Google's continuous integration system
records.licence: unknown (Google Testing Blog, no reuse licence stated on page)
records.finding: Flakiness is predicted by test size rather than by author discipline: across roughly 4.2 million tests, likelihood of flakiness rose broadly linearly with binary size and with the number of dependencies, and heavier harnesses such as device emulators were the worst offenders. The cheapest flake control is therefore keeping tests small and reducing what they touch, not adding retries.
records.applicability_limits: Correlational analysis of one company's corpus, no causal claim and no released dataset; the size effect is confounded with the kind of behaviour large tests cover, and the tool-specific findings are tied to 2017 emulators.
records.counter_evidence: Testcontainers (EV-0093) and Kent C. Dodds (EV-0094) both push work towards larger, more integrated tests for confidence, which by this evidence buys that confidence at a higher flake rate.

records.source: FinOps Framework (FinOps Foundation)
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 (attribution to FinOps Foundation required)
records.finding: Cost is governed as a capability model, not a budget line: four domains (understand usage and cost, quantify business value, optimise usage and cost, manage the practice) run through an inform-optimise-operate loop, and the load-bearing precondition is allocation, meaning every unit of spend must be attributable to an owning team before optimisation or chargeback means anything.
records.applicability_limits: Written for organisations with a cloud bill large enough to fund a practice; the 2026 revision widens scope to AI, SaaS and data-centre spend but offers no evidence that the capability model changes outcomes. For a small venture only allocation, anomaly detection and unit economics are load-bearing; the maturity ladder is not.
records.counter_evidence: No controlled study links FinOps adoption to lower spend; the framework is consensus practitioner content curated by a vendor-funded foundation.

records.source: OpenTelemetry specification, versioning and stability
records.licence: Apache-2.0 (spec repo); site content CC BY 4.0 per CNCF practice, exact page notice not shown
records.finding: Stability is a per-signal contract, not a project property: signals move through development, stable, deprecated and removed, and only stable signals carry a promise that existing calls keep working across minor versions. Deprecated components keep stable-grade guarantees until removal, so the safe rule is to take long-term dependencies only on stable signals and to pin plus schema-map anything below that.
records.applicability_limits: Governs the OpenTelemetry API, SDK and semantic conventions only; says nothing about whether a given attribute is useful. Does not cover collector configuration compatibility, which has its own churn.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0043 shows the practical limit: GenAI agent conventions were still Development at v1.42.0, so the tiering is honest but a lot of what an agentic estate wants to emit sits below stable.

records.source: DORA, the five key metrics guide
records.study_design: Cross-sectional survey programme, self-reported, clustered into performance groups; not an experiment
records.population: Tens of thousands of software professionals across a decade of annual surveys
records.finding: Delivery health is measured on two axes at once: throughput (deployment frequency, change lead time) and instability (change fail rate, failed deployment recovery time, deployment rework rate). Reporting a throughput number without an instability number is the failure mode the metric set exists to prevent, and DORA's own framing is that speed and stability rise together rather than trading off.
records.applicability_limits: Self-reported survey data with clustered performance groups, so the association is correlational and the benchmark bands do not transfer to a one-person or small-team venture. Rework rate replaced older phrasing in the 2026 revision, so historical comparisons need care.
records.counter_evidence: The VOID work (EV-0211) argues recovery-time means are statistically unsound; SPACE (EV-0210) argues no small metric set captures productivity and warns about gaming.

records.source: PagerDuty Incident Response documentation, postmortem process
records.finding: A postmortem is an owned artefact with a clock: the incident commander names an owner, the review happens within three calendar days for the top severity and five business days for the next, the timeline is reconstructed from evidence (graphs, logs) rather than memory, and follow-up items are filed as tickets by the owner who does not then chase them. Ownership plus deadline plus evidence-backed timeline is what makes the practice repeatable, and being openly licensed it can be reused verbatim, unlike the Google material.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes a rota, severity levels and a ticket tracker; the fixed deadlines are calibrated to a company with dedicated responders. The guidance is process description, not evidence that postmortems reduce recurrence.
records.counter_evidence: Learning-from-incidents research argues that action-item counts are a poor proxy for learning and that shallow root-cause framing suppresses the useful second stories.

records.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability pillar REL09-BP04
records.version_or_commit: Reliability pillar, latest revision as at 2026-08-03
records.licence: AWS documentation terms, all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: A backup is not evidence; a timed, validated restore is. The named anti-patterns are precisely the assumptions people make: assuming a backup exists, assuming it is uncorrupted, assuming restore fits the recovery time objective, and restoring a snapshot without querying the data back out. The practice is to define validation criteria per data source, restore into a fresh location on a schedule, measure elapsed time against RTO and data loss against RPO, and alert when either is missed.
records.applicability_limits: Implementation guidance is AWS-service specific (Backup, RDS point-in-time recovery, Elastic Disaster Recovery); the principle is portable but the automation is not. Says nothing about restore under adversarial conditions such as ransomware or credential loss.

records.source: Atlas migration lint analyzers
records.version_or_commit: docs v1.3 as at 2026-08-03; Atlas OSS plus Pro tiers
records.licence: Apache-2.0 for Atlas community edition; docs terms unknown; some analyzers are Pro-only
records.finding: Migration risk is statically checkable in CI before anything touches a database: analyzers separate destructive change, backward-incompatible change, data-dependent change (a unique constraint that fails only if duplicates exist) and non-linear history (two migration files added out of sequence). Treating those four as distinct classes lets a policy fail the build on the ones that cannot be recovered and merely warn on the rest.
records.applicability_limits: Static analysis cannot see production data distribution, so data-dependent findings remain probabilistic. Defaults are warnings, so the safety only exists once a project configures failures. Part of the analyzer set sits behind the paid tier.

records.source: Principles of Chaos Engineering
records.licence: unknown (no notice on site; source repo on GitHub)
records.finding: Failure testing is framed as an experiment, not a stunt: state a hypothesis about steady-state output before you break anything, vary events that actually happen in the real world, run continuously and automatically rather than as an annual drill, and bound the blast radius. The steady-state hypothesis is what turns a drill into evidence, because a run either falsifies it or does not.
records.applicability_limits: Written for large distributed systems with real production traffic; the production-preference principle is inappropriate where a single tenant carries all the risk. Unchanged since 2019 and offers no measurement of benefit.
records.counter_evidence: The prefer-production principle conflicts with a small venture's obligation to avoid customer-visible harm; a staging or restore-drill variant is the defensible reading.

records.source: Argo Rollouts analysis and progressive delivery
records.finding: A canary promotion is a machine decision against a declared query, not a human vibe check: an analysis template names the metric provider, a success condition and a failure condition, a failure limit tolerates transient noise, and breaching it aborts the rollout and shifts traffic back to the last stable version automatically. The rollback path is therefore part of the deployment object rather than a runbook someone has to find at three in the morning.
records.applicability_limits: Kubernetes-native and needs a traffic router plus a metrics backend; the pattern does not transfer as-is to a single-instance or serverless deployment. Automatic abort protects the serving tier only, not data already written by the canary.

records.source: CNCF TAG App Delivery, Platform Engineering Maturity Model
records.finding: A platform is assessed on five aspects (investment, adoption, interfaces, operations, measurement) across four levels from provisional to optimising, and the model states plainly that the output that matters is the list of things to improve, not the level scored. Adoption is treated as a signal of platform quality: if people route around the golden path, the path is wrong, so voluntary uptake beats mandate.
records.applicability_limits: Written for organisations with a distinct platform team and internal customers; a solo or small venture has no adoption dynamic to measure, so only the interfaces and measurement aspects carry over. Consensus whitepaper, no outcome data.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0058 records the same tension from the other side: golden paths rot without continual gardening, so maturity gained is not maturity kept.

records.source: Parallel Change (expand, migrate, contract), Danilo Sato on martinfowler.com
records.licence: Copyright Martin Fowler, all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: Backwards-incompatible change is made safe by splitting it into three deployable steps: expand (add the new shape alongside the old), migrate (move every caller or row across), contract (delete the old shape once nothing reads it). Each step is independently releasable and independently revertible, which is what makes forward-only migration viable: you never need a down script because no single deploy breaks the previous application version.
records.applicability_limits: Costs a period of dual maintenance and only pays off when deploys are frequent enough to complete all three phases; the named risk is a contract phase that never happens, leaving permanent duplication. Applies to interfaces and schemas, not to irreversible data destruction.

records.source: Flyway documentation, undo migrations
records.version_or_commit: current Redgate Flyway docs, Teams edition feature; inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Redgate documentation terms, all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: The maintainer of the most widely used migration tool says down migrations do not do what people think: they can undo schema but not destructive data change, and they cannot recover a migration that failed part way through a multi-statement script. The recommended strategy is keeping the schema backwards compatible with every application version still in production, so an application rollback needs no database change at all, backed by a tested backup and restore path.
records.applicability_limits: A tool vendor arguing about its own paid feature; the backwards-compatibility advice assumes short-lived version skew and does not address long-running batch jobs holding old assumptions.
records.counter_evidence: Direct disagreement with tools that ship down migrations as a first-class primitive (Atlas down migrations, Rails, Alembic), which treat reversibility as a design goal rather than a trap.

records.source: gh-ost, GitHub online schema migration for MySQL
records.version_or_commit: master, described as GA and stable; inspected 2026-08-03
records.finding: A schema change is treated as a controllable long-running operation rather than a single statement: reading the binary log instead of installing triggers lets the tool be paused for real, throttled under load, trialled against a replica first, and cut over at a moment of the operator's choosing. Testability before the cut-over is the safety property, not the migration speed.
records.applicability_limits: MySQL with row-based binary logging and a replication topology; nothing here applies to PostgreSQL or managed serverless databases. Operational complexity is only justified above a table size where an in-place ALTER would lock too long.

records.source: Piranha, Uber stale feature flag cleanup
records.finding: Flag debt is treated as a mechanical refactoring problem: when a flag reaches its terminal state a tool rewrites the abstract syntax tree to delete the dead branch and raises the cleanup change automatically, so removal happens as a matter of course rather than depending on someone remembering. The design implication is that a flag needs a declared expiry and terminal value at creation time, otherwise the automation has nothing to act on.
records.applicability_limits: Requires per-language grammars and a house flag API the tool can recognise; a small codebase gets most of the benefit from a scheduled report of flags past their expiry date rather than from automated rewriting.

records.source: The SPACE of Developer Productivity (Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck, Butler)
records.study_design: Framework synthesis over prior empirical studies, no new experiment
records.population: Software developers, industry and research settings
records.version_or_commit: ACM Queue vol 19 issue 1, pages 20-48, February 2021
records.licence: ACM copyright; paraphrase only, no verbatim reuse
records.finding: Productivity cannot be read off a single metric or a single dimension. The five dimensions are satisfaction and well-being, performance, activity, communication and collaboration, efficiency and flow, and the practical rule is to measure across at least three of them, mixing system telemetry with perceptual data, because any one number becomes a target and stops being a measure.
records.applicability_limits: Aimed at organisations large enough to run surveys; the perceptual half of SPACE is unavailable to a solo operator, which leaves only the system-telemetry half and reintroduces the single-axis risk the paper warns about.
records.counter_evidence: Sits in tension with the DORA metric set (EV-0199), which is deliberately a small fixed set of delivery numbers; the reconciliation is that DORA measures the delivery system, not the people.

records.source: Moving past simple incident metrics, Courtney Nash on the VOID (InfoQ interview)
records.study_design: Observational analysis of a corpus of public incident reports, plus Monte Carlo simulation of duration data
records.population: Publicly published software incident reports collected in the Verica Open Incident Database
records.finding: Incident duration is positively skewed and highly variable, so a mean time to recovery is arithmetic performed on data that does not support it, and the VOID corpus found no correlation between how long an incident ran and how bad it was. Duration is called gray data: high variability, low fidelity. The recommended substitutes are service level objectives, customer impact, cost of coordination and near-miss reporting, with near-miss reports deliberately kept lightweight and not automatically triggering an investigation.
records.applicability_limits: Corpus is self-selected public reports from organisations willing to publish, which skews towards larger and more mature engineering cultures; the argument is statistical and observational, not causal. Secondary interview source, not the report itself.
records.counter_evidence: Directly contradicts the recovery-time component of the DORA metric set (EV-0199), which retains failed deployment recovery time as a key measure.

records.source: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
records.finding: The ten risks are ordered by observed exploitation rather than theoretical severity, and prompt injection sits at LLM01 while its downstream consequences are catalogued separately as improper output handling, excessive agency and sensitive information disclosure, so a control set has to treat injection as an assumed condition and put the enforcement on the consequences.
records.applicability_limits: A community consensus list built from practitioner reporting, not measurement; it names risk classes and gives no thresholds, no test procedure and no way to tell whether a mitigation is sufficient.
records.counter_evidence: Ranking is by expert vote, so ordering may lag the actual incident distribution for any single deployment shape.

records.source: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
records.finding: Agentic risk is catalogued as ASI01 to ASI10, a separate axis from the LLM list, because the failure unit changes once the system holds goals, credentials, tools, memory and the autonomy to chain them across many steps; the list was assembled from incidents in deployed systems by more than a hundred reviewers rather than from projected threats.
records.applicability_limits: The category names sit behind a document download and were not read in full at this access; the entries describe risk classes for enterprise agent platforms and do not prescribe controls or acceptance thresholds for a single-operator venture.

records.source: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
records.study_design: adaptive, defence-aware attack evaluation against five deployed defence systems
records.population: tool-using LLM agents in simulated email, banking, travel and workspace environments
records.model: Qwen2.5-7B among others
records.licence: arXiv default (author licence not confirmed at access); unknown
records.finding: Deterministic out-of-band enforcement, meaning capabilities, information-flow labels and reference monitors sitting outside the model, held up under defence-aware attack where in-band detection did not: mean attack success fell from 25.8 percent to 4.2 percent under Progent and a hand-crafted adaptive attack reached only 2.6 percent.
records.applicability_limits: The authors call this one small-scale data point on a single small open model and a single benchmark family, and stronger attacks are expected; the numbers do not transfer to a differently shaped agent or a different tool surface.
records.counter_evidence: Earlier work bypassed eight defences with over 50 percent success using adaptive attacks, and static-benchmark results have repeatedly made weaker defences look effective.

records.source: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
records.study_design: adaptive attack evaluation of eight published defences
records.population: tool-using LLM agents
records.model: multiple frontier and open models
records.benchmark: indirect prompt injection benchmarks including AgentDojo-style suites
records.licence: arXiv default (author licence not confirmed at access); unknown
records.finding: All eight defences evaluated were bypassed by attacks tailored to the defence, consistently above 50 percent attack success, so any claimed detection or refusal rate measured against a fixed attack set is an upper bound with no lower bound at all.
records.applicability_limits: Attacks were tailored with knowledge of each defence, which models a determined adversary rather than opportunistic web content; the study predates the 2026 out-of-band defence generation.
records.counter_evidence: The 2026 adaptive-evaluation follow-up finds out-of-band enforcement substantially harder to break than the in-band defences broken here.

records.source: CaMeL: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
records.study_design: system design plus benchmark evaluation with provable security claims
records.population: tool-using LLM agents
records.model: frontier models behind a planner and quarantined interpreter
records.finding: Extract control flow and data flow from the trusted user query up front, run untrusted data through an interpreter that cannot alter that flow, and attach capabilities so security policy is checked at the point of tool invocation; this solved 77 percent of tasks against 84 percent undefended, which prices the security tax at roughly seven points of utility.
records.applicability_limits: The approach needs the task to be expressible as a plan before untrusted data is seen, so open-ended tasks degrade badly; independent evaluation reports zero utility for the static strategy on fully open-ended benchmarks.
records.counter_evidence: Follow-up work notes CaMeL's static planning yields zero utility on open-ended agent tasks, so the guarantee is bought by narrowing the task class.

records.source: AgentDojo
records.study_design: dynamic benchmark environment measuring utility and security jointly
records.population: LLM agents managing email, e-banking, travel booking and workspace tools
records.model: multiple frontier models
records.licence: arXiv default (author licence not confirmed at access); unknown
records.finding: Security has to be scored against utility on the same runs, because a defence that refuses work scores perfectly on attack success and is useless; the benchmark also shows agents failing many tasks with no attacker present at all, so baseline competence and security are not separable measurements.
records.applicability_limits: A simulated environment with synthetic tool suites and a fixed attack corpus, so absolute rates do not transfer; results age as models change and as attackers adapt.

records.source: Model Context Protocol security best practices
records.version_or_commit: spec revision 2025-11-25 (page served current revision when the 2025-06-18 path was requested)
records.licence: MIT (Model Context Protocol specification repository); unknown for the rendered site
records.finding: The tool boundary carries hard requirements, not advice: servers must not accept tokens not issued to them, must not use sessions for authentication, must implement per-client consent before proxying a third-party authorisation, must use non-deterministic session identifiers, clients must reject non-http schemes in authorisation URLs and must not open URLs through a shell, and one-click local server installation must show the exact command before executing it.
records.applicability_limits: Written for the OAuth and transport surface of MCP deployments; it does not address what a correctly authorised tool then does with untrusted content, and the strongest statements assume a hosted server rather than a local stdio one.

records.source: The lethal trifecta for AI agents (Simon Willison)
records.finding: Exfiltration needs three properties at once, access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and the ability to communicate outwards, so the cheapest reliable control is a configuration rule that no single agent context holds all three, rather than a filter; a guardrail advertised at 95 percent is a failing grade against an adversary who retries.
records.applicability_limits: A framing device from a practitioner blog with no measurement behind it; it says which configurations are unsafe and nothing about how to make a configuration that needs all three safe.
records.counter_evidence: Out-of-band enforcement work argues a policy layer can mediate all three safely for constrained task classes, which the trifecta rule would forbid outright.
records.licence_evidence: Page fetched at 200/27KB with a browser user agent. The raw HTML contains zero occurrences of the string "licence"/"license" and no Creative Commons badge or link. The footer carries archive/tag links only, with no rights statement.

records.source: Claude Code sandboxed Bash tool documentation
records.version_or_commit: docs current at access; features cited require Claude Code v2.1.216 and v2.1.219
records.finding: Containment is enforced by the operating system on the running process, so it holds regardless of what the model chose to run, and it only works as a pair: filesystem isolation without egress control lets a compromised run exfiltrate keys, egress control without filesystem isolation lets it rewrite the settings that define its own policy. Egress defaults to no allowed domains, credential files and secret environment variables are only protected if listed, and the vendor states plainly that the sandbox is not a complete isolation boundary.
records.applicability_limits: Not available on native Windows, incompatible with docker and some Go CLIs, and the default proxy does not terminate TLS so a broad allowlist entry such as github.com remains an exfiltration path; the sandbox covers Bash subprocesses only, not the in-process file and fetch tools.
records.licence_evidence: Raw HTML fetched at 200/715KB contains zero occurrences of the string "licence"/"license". The page is documentation prose on the sandboxed Bash tool with no rights, licence or terms statement.

records.source: Gitleaks
records.version_or_commit: unknown (repo head at access, 28.5k stars); maintainer declares the project feature complete with security patches only, successor named Betterleaks
records.finding: Secret detection is cheap enough to run as a pre-commit hook and again in CI, with regex plus entropy rules, a committed baseline for known findings and SARIF output so the same rule set feeds local and pipeline enforcement; the cost of a miss is rotation, so detection is a backstop for prevention rather than the control itself.
records.applicability_limits: Regex and entropy detection produces false positives and misses novel credential shapes, it does not verify whether a matched credential is live, and the project has stopped taking features, so pinning it is a decision with a known end of life.
records.review: on-change-of:gitleaks maintenance status or Betterleaks release

records.source: GitHub secret scanning push protection
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 (GitHub Docs content licence); unknown for product behaviour
records.finding: The block sits on the push path and covers the command line, the web UI, file upload, the REST API and MCP server writes on public repositories, so it catches the agent that commits round the hook; bypass is allowed but must carry a stated reason and raises an alert and an audit event, which turns an override into a recorded decision rather than a silent one.
records.applicability_limits: Platform-specific and gated behind GitHub Secret Protection, it only matches provider patterns it knows, and the free path for users covers public repositories only; it is a server-side backstop and does nothing for secrets that never reach GitHub.

records.source: Threat Modeling Manifesto
records.version_or_commit: unknown (no version or revision date stated on the page)
records.finding: Value the practice of finding and fixing design issues over compliance checkboxes, run it early and often on manageable portions of the system rather than as one grand model, and judge it by whether stakeholders get value; the named anti-patterns are the hero threat modeller, admiring the problem without fixing it, overfocus that loses the big picture and the search for a perfect representation.
records.applicability_limits: A values document authored by practitioners with no method, no notation and no evidence of outcome improvement; it tells you how to hold the practice, not what threats to look for.

records.source: Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool threat categories (STRIDE)
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Microsoft Learn documentation); unknown for the tool
records.finding: STRIDE gives six prompts, spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation of privilege, each the negation of a property you wanted; the value is that a non-specialist can generate pointed questions per element of a data-flow diagram, which makes the method teachable and repeatable rather than dependent on a security expert.
records.applicability_limits: Tied to a data-flow view of classic client-server systems and to a Microsoft tool from 2017; it has no vocabulary for a model that follows instructions found in the data it reads, so agentic threats need a supplementary catalogue.

records.source: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
records.version_or_commit: 2025 c. 18, as enacted; data protection provisions commencing in phases to 19 June 2026
records.finding: UK data protection duties now include a statutory complaints route for data subjects at section 103, a seventh lawful basis of recognised legitimate interests at Schedule 4 and reworked automated decision-making rules at section 80 and Schedule 6, so a small venture needs a named complaints path and a recorded lawful basis, not just a privacy notice.
records.applicability_limits: Statute rather than guidance, so it states duties without telling a two-person venture what proportionate evidence of compliance looks like; commencement is phased, and the ICO guidance interpreting it was still being published through 2026. The ICO's own pages refused automated access at this cutoff, so interpretation here rests on the Act plus secondary reporting.
records.review: on-change-of:ICO guidance for the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025

records.source: NCSC Small Business Guide to Cyber Security
records.population: UK small organisations
records.version_or_commit: collection with a stated review date of 21 July 2026
records.licence: Open Government Licence (typical for NCSC); unknown exact
records.finding: The national baseline for a small organisation is deliberately five topics deep, covering backups, device protection, account protection, phishing awareness and malware, on the reasoning that a short list actually done beats a long list partly done.
records.applicability_limits: Only the first of six pages was retrievable at this access, so the per-topic actions were not read in full; the guide targets office IT hygiene for a small business and says nothing about software supply chain or agent tooling.
records.review: on-change-of:NCSC small organisations guide review date

records.source: IBM Carbon Design System (monorepo)
records.version_or_commit: unknown release tag; 14,480 commits on main, repo updated 2026-08-02 at inspection
records.finding: Dense enterprise systems ship the whole production kit as one versioned monorepo, tokens, Sass, React and web components, icons and grid together, because the binding constraint is cross-product consistency across many long-lived internal apps rather than visual novelty.
records.applicability_limits: Sized for a large vendor with dedicated system staff and a single corporate brand; the grid and token surface is heavy for a small product and the visual language reads as IBM unless retokenised.
records.counter_evidence: shadcn/ui (EV-0067) shows the opposite distribution model, copy-and-own source rather than a versioned dependency, works better for small teams.

records.source: Microsoft Fluent UI (web repo)
records.version_or_commit: Fluent UI React v9 current, v8 and v0 still maintained; 20,701 commits on master at inspection
records.licence: MIT for repository code; fonts and icons under a separate assets licence agreement
records.finding: A system at estate scale must support gradual migration as a first-class feature: v9, v8 and v0 components are documented as composable in one app, so a major redesign becomes an incremental swap rather than a rewrite gate.
records.applicability_limits: Multi-generation coexistence costs bundle size, theming complexity and reviewer confusion; it earns its keep only when the consuming estate is too large to migrate atomically.
records.counter_evidence: Shopify archived Polaris React outright (EV-0238) rather than carrying two generations, showing a clean-break alternative.

records.source: Fluent 2 design language site
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live doc, inspected 2026-08-03; footer shows Microsoft 2026)
records.licence: Proprietary, Microsoft terms of use; no open licence offered for the guidance
records.finding: One design language is stated across web, iOS, Android and Windows, so the portable asset is the token and behaviour layer while each platform keeps its native chrome, and accessibility is tooled at design time through focus-order and contrast plugins rather than checked only at the end.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor marketing surface with no versioning or changelog visible, and the cross-platform claim is not backed by published research on the site.
records.counter_evidence: Apple HIG (EV-0230) argues the opposite emphasis, that platform conventions should dominate a house language on Apple platforms.

records.source: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live doc, inspected 2026-08-03; body is script-rendered and was not retrievable by plain fetch, principles confirmed only through secondary summaries)
records.licence: Proprietary, Apple copyright; freely readable, not reusable
records.finding: Mobile-native design is treated as conformance to platform conventions, clarity, deference to content and depth as layered hierarchy, so on Apple platforms the correct default is the system control with system behaviour, and house style is applied inside those controls.
records.applicability_limits: Primary page body could not be fetched, so the principle statement rests on secondary sources and should be re-verified before it is quoted in pack content; guidance is Apple-platform specific and is revised each OS generation without a stable version handle.
records.counter_evidence: Material 3 Expressive research (EV-0232) reports measurable gains from deliberately breaking restrained convention, though within its own platform.

records.source: Material Web components
records.version_or_commit: unknown release; 5,152 commits on main at inspection, repo states maintenance mode pending new maintainers
records.finding: A platform vendor's reference implementation can be parked while the guidance it implements keeps moving, so a system's dependency choice must be justified against maintenance signals in the repo, not against the brand behind the guidance.
records.applicability_limits: Maintenance mode concerns this web component package only, not Material guidance or the Android and Angular implementations; status can change if maintainers appear.
records.counter_evidence: Material guidance itself is actively promoted and researched (EV-0232), which is exactly why brand-level trust misleads here.

records.source: Expressive Material Design, Google research write-up
records.study_design: Vendor-run programme of 46 studies over about three years, mixing eye tracking, surveys, focus groups and usability tests; no protocol, pre-registration or statistics published
records.population: Reported as over 18,000 participants internationally, composition not disclosed
records.licence: Proprietary, Google copyright; no reuse licence stated
records.finding: Expressive styling is not merely decorative: emphasis through size, shape, containment and colour reportedly let people find key targets up to four times faster and closed the age gap for users over 45, while preference gains were strongest among 18 to 24 year olds at 87 per cent.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor-run, unpublished and unreviewed, measured on Google's own surfaces, and the article itself notes gains were dampened by unfamiliarity and that breaking established patterns harmed usability in some tests; treat as directional, not as a controlled result.
records.counter_evidence: Nielsen Norman Group argues restrained flat styling already erodes discoverability (EV-0234), the mirror-image claim from equally weak evidence.

records.source: Nielsen Norman Group, 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
records.study_design: Heuristics derived in 1990 and refined by factor analysis of 249 usability problems, published 1994; article last reviewed 2024-01-30
records.population: Usability problems catalogued by the authors, not a user sample
records.version_or_commit: 1994 heuristic set, page last reviewed 2024-01-30, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Copyright Jakob Nielsen; reuse of the heuristics permitted with credit and a link to the page
records.finding: A small fixed vocabulary of ten broad heuristics gives reviewers a shared language for naming interface defects, which is why heuristic review is cheap and repeatable even where it is not predictive.
records.applicability_limits: A 1994 factor analysis of one problem catalogue is not evidence that following the heuristics improves outcomes, and the source is a consultancy selling training on them; use as review vocabulary, never as a conformance claim.
records.counter_evidence: WCAG 2.2 (EV-0027) shows the contrasting model, individually testable success criteria with a defined conformance meaning.

records.source: Nielsen Norman Group, Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems
records.study_design: Opinion piece with one anecdotal user quote and unlinked references to in-house research; no sample size or method reported
records.version_or_commit: published 2015-09-27, no later revision shown, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Copyright 1998-2026 Nielsen Norman Group, all rights reserved
records.finding: Stripping visual signifiers costs discoverability: if a control does not look actionable, people hunt for it, so any minimal system must pay back the removed affordance with an explicit interaction-state contract.
records.applicability_limits: Eleven years old, evidence is anecdotal and the claim is asserted rather than measured; usable as a hypothesis to test, not as a finding to cite as fact.
records.counter_evidence: Google's expressive research (EV-0232) reaches a compatible conclusion by a different route, but both sit at the same weak evidence grade.

records.source: WebAIM Million 2026
records.study_design: Automated census: WAVE stand-alone API run against the rendered DOM of the top one million home pages from the Tranco ranking, eighth annual edition
records.population: 1,000,000 home pages analysed February 2026
records.licence: Copyright 2026 WebAIM, Utah State University; no reuse licence stated
records.finding: Accessibility failure is concentrated in a handful of cheap defects, low-contrast text on 83.9 per cent of pages, missing alt text 53.1, unlabelled inputs 51.0, empty links 46.3, empty buttons 30.6 and undeclared page language 13.5, and it is getting worse, 95.9 per cent of pages failing and 56.1 errors per page as pages grew 22.5 per cent in elements in a year.
records.applicability_limits: Home pages only, automated detection only, and the report states plainly that no detected errors does not mean a page is accessible; the six-item profile is a floor to automate, not a definition of accessible.
records.counter_evidence: axe-core (EV-0236) puts automated coverage at about 57 per cent of WCAG issues, so the true failure rate exceeds the measured one.

records.source: axe-core
records.version_or_commit: unknown release tag; 5,495 commits on develop at inspection, minor releases stated every three to five months
records.licence: MPL-2.0 for axe-core; bundled dependencies under their own terms
records.finding: The maintainer scopes its own tool honestly, about 57 per cent of WCAG issues found automatically, with an explicit incomplete state for checks it cannot decide, so a machine gate should assert zero violations plus a human verdict on the incomplete list.
records.applicability_limits: Rule coverage spans WCAG 2.0 to 2.2 at A to AAA plus non-normative best-practice rules, so a raw pass or fail conflates standard conformance with house opinion unless tags are pinned; colour contrast does not work under JSDOM, so checks need a real browser.
records.counter_evidence: Storybook docs (EV-0104) repeat the common lower figure of roughly a third for automated coverage, so the 57 per cent claim is a vendor high-water mark.

records.source: Overlay Fact Sheet
records.study_design: Consensus statement, no study; 1,031 signatories at inspection including WCAG and ARIA contributors, screen reader developers and disabled users
records.licence: unknown (no licence or copyright notice shown)
records.finding: Bolt-on accessibility overlays cannot deliver conformance, cannot repair alt text, labels, keyboard access or scripted content, and sniffing assistive-technology use exposes disability status without consent, so accessibility must be built into components rather than bought as a script tag.
records.applicability_limits: Advocacy consensus rather than a controlled comparison, and many signatories work in accessibility consultancy which competes with overlay vendors; the technical claims are nonetheless checkable against WCAG.
records.counter_evidence: None found at comparable standing; overlay vendors dispute it but publish no independent evaluation.

records.source: Shopify Polaris React
records.version_or_commit: archived read-only on 2026-01-06; Polaris Web Components released 2025-10-01 as successor
records.licence: Custom MIT-based licence limited to applications that integrate with Shopify software or services; icons and images under the Polaris Design Guidelines licence
records.finding: Two independent lessons: a house system can be openly published yet legally unusable outside its ecosystem, and a vendor can retire a framework-bound implementation in favour of framework-agnostic web components, so licence text and delivery technology are adoption decisions, not details.
records.applicability_limits: Merchant-admin domain with a captive audience of app developers, so the licence restriction carries no cost for Shopify and would be fatal for a system seeking outside adoption.
records.counter_evidence: Fluent (EV-0228) chose multi-generation coexistence over a clean break for a comparably large estate.

records.source: Guardian csnx monorepo, home of the Source design system
records.version_or_commit: unknown package versions; 2,955 commits on main at inspection
records.finding: An editorial system keeps its component surface deliberately small and centres typography, measure and article furniture, because the product is reading rather than task completion, and it ships alongside the consent and analytics packages that share the page budget.
records.applicability_limits: Small repo audience and no published component criteria comparable to GOV.UK, so treat it as a shape-of-system exemplar and not as governance guidance; typographic choices are brand-specific.
records.counter_evidence: GOV.UK (EV-0062, EV-0103) shows a far heavier evidence gate for admitting components, which an editorial pace would not tolerate.

records.source: Grafana dashboard best practices
records.version_or_commit: unknown (latest docs channel, inspected 2026-08-03; no page date shown)
records.licence: unknown (no licence or copyright statement on the page)
records.finding: A data-heavy surface is judged by whether it answers one named question under stress, so a dashboard commits to a method such as RED, USE or the four golden signals, orders panels as a narrative and carries its own written context, rather than displaying every available metric.
records.applicability_limits: Written for infrastructure observability with an on-call reader; business and analytics dashboards have different urgency and audience, and the page is vendor guidance with no evaluation behind it.
records.counter_evidence: None found; the conflicting practice, exhaustive metric walls, is common in the wild but undefended in published guidance.

records.source: web.dev, how Core Web Vitals affect business metrics
records.study_design: Collected vendor and partner case studies, mostly before-and-after correlations; the page itself recommends A/B testing as the only meaningful measurement
records.population: Named commercial sites including Vodafone, Tokopedia, redBus, Nykaa and iCook
records.finding: Conversion-led surfaces should treat field performance as a design constraint with a money number attached, such as Vodafone's reported 31 per cent LCP improvement alongside 8 per cent more sales, and should prove the link by experiment rather than by assertion.
records.applicability_limits: Correlational case studies chosen by an interested party, no confidence intervals or controls, and the page has not been updated since 2021 while the metric set has changed, INP having replaced FID; use the method, not the numbers.
records.counter_evidence: The page's own Vodafone note concedes that only A/B testing measures meaningful impact, which undercuts the headline figures it lists.

records.source: Barnett, Kurniawan, Thudumu, Brannelly and Abdelrazek, Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System (CAIN 2024)
records.study_design: Experience report across three independently built RAG systems in research, education and biomedical domains, failure points induced from operational defects rather than from a controlled benchmark
records.population: Three production or near-production RAG deployments built by the authors and collaborators
records.finding: RAG failures cluster at seven named seams and most of them sit outside the model: missing content, top-k cut-off dropping a document that was retrieved, consolidation losing a document that survived retrieval, extraction failing on a document that reached the prompt, wrong output format, wrong specificity, and incompleteness. The two structural claims matter more than the taxonomy: a RAG system can only be validated during operation because the failure distribution depends on the live corpus and live queries, and robustness is accumulated by responding to observed failures rather than designed in at the start.
records.applicability_limits: Three case studies by one group, no control condition and no statistical claim, so the seven points are a checklist of seams to instrument, not a measured frequency distribution. Written before widely available million-token contexts and before agentic retrieval loops became normal, so the top-k and consolidation seams may present differently when the retriever is a tool call inside an agent. Says nothing about which mitigation works.
records.counter_evidence: The claim that validation is only feasible during operation is in tension with EV-0255 and EV-0087, which both argue offline evaluation sets with error bars can and should gate a release. The honest reading is that offline evals gate change and production telemetry discovers the next failure class.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page carries the licence block <div class="abs-license"><a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" title="Rights to this article" class="has_license"> with the by-4.0.png badge and the link text "view license". Paper: "Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System". Verified in raw HTML, not only via the rendered summary.

records.source: Liu, Lin, Hewitt, Paranjape, Bevilacqua, Petroni and Liang, Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (TACL vol 12, 157-173, 2024)
records.study_design: Controlled positional manipulation: the position of the single relevant document is varied inside an otherwise fixed context on multi-document question answering and synthetic key-value retrieval
records.population: Open and closed models available in 2023, including explicitly long-context variants
records.model: GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k, Claude 1.3 and 1.3-100k, MPT-30B-Instruct, LongChat-13B
records.benchmark: NaturalQuestions-Open multi-document QA, synthetic key-value retrieval
records.version_or_commit: TACL 2024 version of record, DOI 10.1162/tacl_a_00638; arXiv:2307.03172
records.finding: Position inside the context is a first-class variable, not a formatting detail. Accuracy is highest when the needed evidence sits at the very start or very end of the context and degrades markedly when it sits in the middle, and this holds for models explicitly sold as long-context. The decision rule is that context ordering is part of the system design: put the load-bearing evidence at the edges, and treat a longer context window as a licence to include more, not as a guarantee that everything included will be used.
records.applicability_limits: Models tested are all 2023 vintage and long since retired, so the magnitude of the effect must be re-measured per model rather than assumed. Tasks are single-needle retrieval and short-answer QA, which do not represent synthesis, code editing or agent trajectories. The study does not test whether instructing the model about position, or repeating evidence, removes the effect.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0244 finds the degradation is not a clean U-shape once distractors and needle-question similarity are varied, so the tidy lost-in-the-middle curve is one slice of a messier surface.
records.review: on-change-of:a replication on a current frontier model class
records.licence_evidence: Page carries <a rel=license href=http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/> with the CC BY 4.0 badge image, and the footer states: "Materials prior to 2016 here are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 International License... Materials published in or after 2016 are licensed on a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License." This paper ("Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts") is 2024, so the CC BY 4.0 branch applies.

records.source: Hong, Troynikov and Huber (Chroma), Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
records.study_design: Vendor technical report: controlled extensions of needle-in-a-haystack varying input length, needle-question semantic similarity, distractor presence, haystack structure, plus a text replication task
records.population: Eighteen models across major families
records.model: GPT-4.1 family, Claude 4 family, Gemini 2.5 family, Qwen3 family and others
records.version_or_commit: Technical report dated 14 July 2025; replication toolkit at github.com/chroma-core/context-rot
records.finding: Models do not use their context uniformly, and the failure is not a function of length alone. Reliability falls as input grows even on tasks that are trivially easy at short length: one model family dropped 30 to 45 per cent as irrelevant context grew from about 300 tokens to about 113,000. The fall is modulated by how semantically close the needle is to the question, whether plausible distractors are present, and how the haystack is structured, and coherent well-structured haystacks degraded attention more than shuffled ones. Advertised window size is therefore a capacity limit, not a working limit: a 200k window can show serious loss well before 200k. The decision rule is to measure the usable context length for your own task and pin a budget below it, rather than filling the window because it is there.
records.applicability_limits: Published by a retrieval vendor whose product benefits if long context looks unreliable, so the direction of the incentive is worth naming even though the toolkit is open for replication. Not peer reviewed. Model versions tested are already superseded, so the numbers age fast even if the shape of the effect does not. It measures retrieval and replication, not multi-step agentic work.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0245 found long-context prompting beat retrieval on average when resources allowed, which cuts against a strong reading that long context is simply unusable.
records.licence_evidence: The given URL 301-redirects to https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot. That page fetched at 200/281KB and contains zero occurrences of the string "licence"/"license". Footer shows only "© 2026" with Privacy and Terms links, naming no content licence.

records.source: Li, Yan, Wang, Le, Zhu, Wang, Zhu, Pham, Chen, Wang, Le and Pfister, Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach (EMNLP 2024 Industry Track)
records.study_design: Head-to-head benchmarking of retrieval-augmented prompting against whole-corpus long-context prompting on shared datasets, plus an ablation of a self-reflective router
records.population: Public long-context QA and summarisation datasets
records.model: Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4O, GPT-3.5-Turbo
records.benchmark: LongBench and similar public long-context suites
records.finding: When you can afford the tokens, feeding the long context directly beats retrieval on average quality, and retrieval's advantage is cost rather than accuracy. The two approaches agree on most queries, which is what makes the hybrid work: Self-Route first asks the model whether the retrieved context suffices, answers cheaply when it does, and escalates to full context when it does not, recovering close to long-context quality at close to retrieval cost. The decision rule is to treat retrieval versus long context as a per-query routing decision with a measured escalation rate, not as an architecture chosen once.
records.applicability_limits: Measured on public benchmark corpora that fit in a window at all, so it says nothing about corpora of millions of documents where retrieval is not optional. Cost conclusions are tied to 2024 token prices and predate widespread prompt caching, which changes the arithmetic substantially, see EV-0261. The router depends on the model's own judgement of sufficiency, which inherits the calibration problems described in EV-0250.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0244 and EV-0243 both show long-context reading degrades in ways average benchmark scores hide, so an average-quality win can coexist with worse tail behaviour.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page carries the licence block <div class="abs-license"><a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" title="Rights to this article" class="has_license"> with the by-4.0.png badge and the link text "view license". Paper: "Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach". Verified in raw HTML.

records.source: Thakur, Reimers, Ruckle, Srivastava and Gurevych, BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models (NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks Track)
records.study_design: Zero-shot benchmark across eighteen heterogeneous retrieval datasets, ten retrieval architectures evaluated without in-domain training
records.population: Bio-medical, financial, scientific, argument, news and community question answering corpora
records.benchmark: BEIR, eighteen datasets, nDCG@10 primary metric
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:2104.08663v4, 21 October 2021; reference implementation github.com/beir-cellar/beir, Apache-2.0
records.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (arXiv posting); Apache-2.0 for the beir-cellar reference implementation
records.finding: Out of domain, lexical BM25 is a strong and hard-to-beat baseline, re-ranking and late-interaction models win on quality at high computational cost, and dense bi-encoders often lose to BM25 despite winning in-domain. The decision rule for a venture is that the first retrieval implementation should be BM25 or a hybrid with BM25, embeddings must earn their place against that baseline on your own corpus, and any reranker must be justified against its latency cost.
records.applicability_limits: Benchmark predates modern instruction-tuned embedding models and modern rerankers, so absolute rankings are stale. It measures retrieval quality in isolation, not end-to-end answer quality, and nDCG@10 does not tell you whether the generator will use the retrieved evidence. Zero-shot generalisation is the whole point of the design, so it under-represents cases where you do have in-domain training data.
records.counter_evidence: Later embedding models have narrowed or reversed the BM25 gap on parts of BEIR, and BEIR itself has been criticised for saturation and for datasets with shallow relevance judgements.
records.review: on-change-of:a successor heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark with current embedding models

records.source: Niu, Wu, Zhu, Xu, Shum, Zhong, Song and Zhang, RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models (ACL 2024)
records.study_design: Corpus construction with manual word-level and case-level hallucination annotation, followed by benchmarking of detection methods and of a fine-tuned detector
records.population: Nearly 18,000 naturally generated RAG responses across question answering, data-to-text and news summarisation
records.model: Multiple contemporary open and closed generators used to produce the annotated responses
records.finding: Retrieval reduces hallucination but does not remove it: models still produce claims unsupported by, or contradicting, the very context they were given, and the rate varies sharply between generators on identical retrieved context. Because the annotation is word-level, groundedness is measurable as a span-level property rather than as a whole-response verdict, and a fine-tuned detector trained on such annotations can outperform prompting a large model to judge groundedness. The decision rule is to measure groundedness against the retrieved context as a separate metric from answer correctness, since a system can be right and ungrounded or grounded and wrong.
records.applicability_limits: Generators annotated are 2023 to 2024 vintage, so absolute hallucination rates do not transfer. Three task families only, none of them agentic or tool-using. Word-level annotation is expensive, so the method transfers as a principle but a small venture will not reproduce the corpus scale. Says nothing about hallucination in the retrieval step itself.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0250 argues the incentive structure of evaluation, not the retrieval architecture, is the dominant driver of confident wrong answers, which implies detection alone will not fix the rate.
records.licence_evidence: Page carries <a rel=license href=http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/> with the CC BY 4.0 badge image, and the footer states: "Materials published in or after 2016 are licensed on a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License." This paper ("RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models") is 2024, so the CC BY 4.0 branch applies.

records.source: Ovadia, Brief, Mishaeli and Elisha (Microsoft), Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs (EMNLP 2024)
records.study_design: Controlled comparison of unsupervised fine-tuning against retrieval augmentation for injecting both new and existing factual knowledge, same base models and same evaluation sets
records.population: Knowledge-intensive multiple-choice tasks plus a current-events set constructed after the training cutoff
records.model: Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, Orca2-7B
records.benchmark: MMLU task subsets, a purpose-built current-events dataset
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:2312.05934, December 2023; EMNLP 2024 main conference version
records.finding: For getting facts into a system, retrieval beat unsupervised fine-tuning in almost every condition tested, including for facts the base model had never seen. Models struggle to acquire new factual content from continued unsupervised training, and exposure to many paraphrases of the same fact partially helps. The decision rule follows: fine-tuning is for form, style, format adherence and task shape, retrieval is for facts, and a plan that proposes fine-tuning to teach the model your data should be challenged before it is funded.
records.applicability_limits: Seven-billion-parameter open models only, so it does not settle the question for frontier-scale models or for supervised instruction fine-tuning on curated question-answer pairs, which is a different intervention from the unsupervised continued pretraining tested here. Multiple-choice evaluation rewards recognition rather than generation. Does not test the combination of both, which is what most production systems actually do.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0249 shows fine-tuning does move capability in target domains when the data regime is large, so the finding is about knowledge injection specifically, not about fine-tuning in general.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page carries the licence block <div class="abs-license"><a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" title="Rights to this article" class="has_license"> with the by-4.0.png badge and the link text "view license". Paper: "Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs". Verified in raw HTML.

records.source: Biderman, Portes, Gonzalez Ortiz and colleagues, LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less (TMLR 2024, Featured Certification)
records.study_design: Controlled comparison of LoRA against full fine-tuning across two target domains and two data regimes, instruction fine-tuning at roughly 100K pairs and continued pretraining at 20B tokens, with forgetting measured on out-of-domain tasks
records.population: Code and mathematics target domains
records.model: Llama-2-7B and Llama-2-13B
records.benchmark: HumanEval, GSM8K, plus out-of-domain retention tasks
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:2405.09673; TMLR 2024 accepted version; artefacts at github.com/danbider/lora-tradeoffs
records.finding: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is a trade, not a free lunch. At standard ranks LoRA learns the target domain substantially less well than full fine-tuning, and in exchange it preserves base-model behaviour outside the target domain better than weight decay or dropout do, and keeps generations more diverse. The decision rule is to pick the method by which risk dominates: if the danger is losing general capability and behavioural stability, take LoRA and accept a weaker fit, and if the danger is failing to reach the required domain quality, do not expect LoRA to close the gap by tuning the rank alone.
records.applicability_limits: Two model sizes, one family, two domains, and 2024 training recipes. The forgetting result is measured on benchmark retention, not on the qualitative behaviours a product cares about such as tone or refusal behaviour. Does not cover current preference-optimisation methods or the mixed adapter-plus-prompt setups common now.
records.counter_evidence: Later work reports the gap narrows with better hyperparameters, higher ranks and more careful optimiser choice, so the size of the deficit is contested even where its direction is not.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page carries the licence block <div class="abs-license"><a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" title="Rights to this article" class="has_license"> with the by-4.0.png badge and the link text "view license". Paper: "LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less". Verified in raw HTML.

records.source: Kalai, Nachum, Vempala and Zhang (OpenAI and Georgia Tech), Why Language Models Hallucinate
records.study_design: Theoretical analysis reducing generative error to binary classification, with an accompanying argument about scoring incentives in mainstream benchmarks
records.finding: Hallucination is partly structural and partly an incentive problem. Statistical pressure during pretraining makes some error rate unavoidable for any model that generalises beyond its data, and post-training keeps the rate high because near-universal binary scoring rewards a guess over an admission of uncertainty. The actionable half is the incentive half: if your own evaluation scores an abstention the same as a wrong answer, you are training and selecting for confident error. The decision rule is that every scoring rubric a venture writes must give explicit credit for calibrated abstention and must record the abstention rate alongside accuracy.
records.applicability_limits: A theoretical argument by the lab that ships one of the models, not an experiment, and the formal result is about existence of error, not about the rate any particular product will see. It does not tell you the right abstention threshold, and pushing abstention too hard produces a useless system that refuses. It does not cover hallucination that arises from a bad retrieved context rather than from the model.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0247 shows a large share of RAG hallucination is contradiction of supplied context, which is a grounding failure rather than an uncertainty-scoring failure, so the incentive story is not the whole account.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page carries the licence block <div class="abs-license"><a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" title="Rights to this article" class="has_license"> with the by-4.0.png badge and the link text "view license". Paper: "Why Language Models Hallucinate". Verified in raw HTML.

records.source: Zheng, Chiang, Sheng and colleagues, Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks Track)
records.study_design: Agreement study between strong model judges and human preferences on a controlled multi-turn question set and on crowdsourced pairwise battles, with named bias analyses
records.population: Expert and crowdsourced human raters, multi-turn open-ended prompts
records.model: GPT-4 as judge; a range of contemporary chat models as subjects
records.finding: A strong model judge reaches roughly eighty per cent or more agreement with human preference, which is about the level two humans reach with each other, so LLM-as-judge is a defensible substitute for human preference rating at scale. The same paper names the failure modes that make an unaudited judge worthless: position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement bias and weak reasoning on tasks requiring calculation. The decision rule is that a judge is a measuring instrument and must be calibrated like one, with randomised or swapped ordering, length controls, and a held-out human-labelled sample reported as agreement.
records.applicability_limits: Agreement is measured on general chat preference, not on domain-specific correctness where the judge lacks the knowledge to grade. Eighty per cent human agreement also means twenty per cent disagreement, which is far too coarse to gate a safety property. The subject and judge models are long retired, so the agreement figure must be re-established for any current judge rather than cited as a constant.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0252 finds position bias is severe and inconsistent enough to change conclusions, and EV-0253 shows self-preference is grounded in genuine self-recognition, both of which make the headline agreement number look optimistic.
records.review: on-change-of:a replication of judge-human agreement on a current frontier judge
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page licence line links "view license" to http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/ (title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena)

records.source: Shi, Sun, Xing and colleagues, Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
records.study_design: Systematic measurement of position bias across judges, tasks and answer pairs, introducing repetition-stability, position-consistency and preference-fairness measures
records.population: Multiple judge models over multiple pairwise comparison tasks
records.model: A range of contemporary judge models
records.benchmark: MTBench and DevBench derived pairwise comparisons
records.finding: Position bias is not a small correction. Which answer a judge prefers depends measurably on which slot the answer occupies, the size of the effect varies by judge and by task rather than being a fixed offset, and it is largest exactly where the two answers are close in quality, which is where evaluations are used to make decisions. The decision rule is that any pairwise judge protocol must run both orderings and treat order-inconsistent pairs as ties or as a reported disagreement rate, and that a judge whose position-consistency is not measured cannot be used to accept or reject a change.
records.applicability_limits: Pairwise comparison only, so it does not directly govern single-answer rubric scoring, which has its own biases. Judge models tested are 2024 vintage. The proposed metrics are useful but not standardised, so numbers are not comparable across papers.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0251 reports GPT-4 suffered less position bias than weaker judges, which suggests the effect shrinks with judge capability even if it does not vanish.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page shows a Creative Commons licence icon with "view license" linking to http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/ (title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge)

records.source: Panickssery, Bowman and Feng, LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations (NeurIPS 2024)
records.study_design: Self-recognition and self-preference measured on the same models, with a fine-tuning intervention used to vary self-recognition and observe the effect on self-preference
records.population: Summarisation outputs from models and from humans
records.model: GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Llama 2
records.finding: Models can distinguish their own output from other models' and from human output at non-trivial accuracy, and that self-recognition capability causally drives the tendency to score their own output above others' when humans rate the outputs as equal. The decision rule is hard: never grade a model's output with the same model where the score selects between candidates, and where a family-mate judge is unavoidable, report the self-preference offset measured on a human-labelled sample rather than assuming it is zero.
records.applicability_limits: Summarisation only, three models, all superseded. The causal manipulation is via fine-tuning self-recognition, which is a proxy for the naturally occurring mechanism rather than the mechanism itself. Says nothing about whether self-preference persists when the judge grades against an explicit rubric with reference answers rather than expressing a preference.
records.counter_evidence: Follow-up work argues some apparent self-preference reflects genuine quality differences that human raters under-detect rather than bias, so the correction direction is not settled.
records.licence_evidence: NeurIPS virtual poster page "LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations" carries no licence or copyright statement; a full-text scan of the rendered page for "licence/license/Creative Commons/copyright/rights reserved" returned zero matches. Footer shows only Privacy Policy, Press, Proceedings and contact links.

records.source: Shankar, Zamfirescu-Pereira, Hartmann, Parameswaran and Arawjo, Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation of LLM Outputs with Human Preferences (UIST 2024)
records.study_design: Mixed-initiative system design plus a qualitative user study of practitioners building evaluators for their own LLM pipelines
records.population: Practitioners building LLM applications, using the EvalGen interface
records.finding: Evaluation criteria are discovered by grading outputs, not written in advance. The study names criteria drift: practitioners cannot fully specify what good looks like until they have seen concrete bad outputs, so the requirements and the evaluator co-evolve, and any workflow that treats the rubric as fixed up front will measure the wrong thing. The decision rule is that a venture grades a small sample by hand first, derives assertions from those grades, and keeps a permanent human-labelled sample against which every later change to the judge is re-validated.
records.applicability_limits: Qualitative study with a small participant pool and a specific research prototype, so the interface findings do not transfer as a product requirement. It describes how alignment work feels and where it fails, not how much accuracy the resulting evaluators achieve. Nothing in it is a controlled measurement.
records.counter_evidence: Nothing directly contradicting, though the emphasis on iterative human grading sits uneasily with the volume of evaluation a fast-shipping venture wants, and EV-0087 is more optimistic about starting from a small fixed set.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page shows "view license" linking to http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (title: Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation of LLM Outputs with Human Preferences)

records.source: Miller (Anthropic), Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
records.study_design: Methodological paper: derives standard errors, clustering corrections, paired-difference tests and power analysis for language model evaluation data
records.finding: An eval is an experiment and must be reported like one. Treat the questions as a sample from an unseen super-population, so a bare percentage without a standard error is not a result; cluster the standard error when questions share a passage or a source; compare models on paired differences on the same questions rather than on independent means, which removes question-difficulty variance and sharply raises power; resample multiple answers per question to cut scoring noise; and run a power analysis before building the set so you know what effect size the eval can even detect. The decision rule for a venture is that a regression gate must state the minimum detectable difference at its chosen sample size, or it is a coin flip dressed as a check.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes independent-ish questions and a scalar score, which fits multiple-choice and pass-fail grading better than open-ended rubric scoring or agent trajectories where the unit of observation is ambiguous. Published by a model vendor. The paired-difference machinery assumes the same question set is run against both models, which breaks when the eval set itself changes between releases. It does not address judge error, which adds a second variance source the paper does not model.
records.counter_evidence: Later work on reporting LLM-as-judge evaluations argues judge error must be propagated into the interval, so the intervals produced by this method alone are too narrow when a model does the grading.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page licence link points to http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/ under "Rights to this article" (title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations)

records.source: Su, Zhang, Ullrich, Bottou and Ibrahim (FAIR at Meta and NYU), A Single Character can Make or Break Your LLM Evals
records.study_design: Controlled variation of the delimiter separating in-context examples, holding content constant, measured across model families and topics, with an attention analysis
records.population: Multiple-choice knowledge evaluation across topics
records.model: Llama, Qwen and Gemma families
records.finding: Changing only the single character used to separate in-context examples moved MMLU scores by up to twenty-three percentage points, enough to put any chosen model at the top of a ranking, and the brittleness did not diminish with scale. Naming the chosen delimiter inside the prompt improved robustness. The decision rule is that a prompt is a versioned artefact whose formatting is load-bearing: pin and record the exact template with any eval result, and treat a model comparison run under different templates as no comparison at all.
records.applicability_limits: Few-shot multiple-choice evaluation on open-weight families; the effect size on instruction-following chat models used zero-shot with structured tool calls is not established here. It measures delimiters specifically, so it is evidence that formatting matters, not a general theory of which formatting choices matter. Preprint, not yet peer reviewed at access date.
records.counter_evidence: None found directly; the direction of the result is consistent with the wider prompt-sensitivity literature, though the magnitude is at the high end of reported effects.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page shows the by-4.0 licence icon (arxiv.org/icons/licenses/by-4.0.png) with "view license" linking to http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (title: A Single Character can Make or Break Your LLM Evals)

records.source: Zhang, Da, Lee, Robinson, Wu and colleagues (Scale AI), A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic (NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track)
records.study_design: Construction of a held-out benchmark (GSM1k) mirroring the style and difficulty of an established public one (GSM8k), then measurement of the performance gap as a contamination signal
records.population: Leading open and closed models as of 2024
records.model: Multiple frontier and open model families
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:2405.00332; NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks version
records.finding: Public benchmark scores are partly a memorisation artefact. Accuracy dropped by up to eight percentage points on a fresh set matched for style and difficulty, systematic overfitting appeared across whole model families, and the size of a model's gap correlated with how readily it could reproduce examples from the original set. Frontier models showed the least of it, and all models still generalised to genuinely novel problems. The decision rule is that a venture must hold out a private evaluation set the model providers have never seen and treat any public benchmark number as an upper bound.
records.applicability_limits: Grade-school arithmetic only, and the measured drop is a contamination signal, not a measure of contamination itself, since a matched set can still differ in ways that explain part of the gap. The specific models are all superseded. The result does not tell you how much of your own product evaluation is contaminated, only that public sets are a poor proxy.
records.counter_evidence: The authors themselves note frontier models showed minimal overfitting, which cuts against a blanket claim that public benchmarks are worthless.
records.licence_evidence: Abstract page shows a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 icon with "view license" linking to http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (title: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic)

records.source: Singh and colleagues (Cohere Labs and collaborators), The Leaderboard Illusion
