records.applicability_limits: Vendor commentary from a single-node warehouse company, and the author states the figures are from memory with the charts hand-drawn, so the numbers are indicative rather than measurements you can cite as data. Nothing here addresses streaming, unstructured data or machine-learning training sets.
records.counter_evidence: The lakehouse position paper argues the opposite direction of travel, that dataset growth and unstructured data broke the warehouse shape. Both cannot be the default; the disagreement is about which population you belong to.

records.source: Johari, Pekelis and Walsh, Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests
records.study_design: Statistical methodology with deployment on a commercial experimentation platform
records.population: Hundreds of thousands of commercial A/B tests
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:1512.04922v3, 16 July 2019; published in Operations Research
records.licence: unknown (arXiv listing; no explicit reuse licence recorded)
records.finding: Peeking is a property of the stopping rule, not of the operator's discipline, so the fix belongs in the statistic rather than in a policy telling people not to look. Always-valid p-values and confidence intervals, built on a mixture sequential probability ratio test, stay valid at every moment, which makes continuous monitoring a supported operation instead of a violation.
records.applicability_limits: Validity at all times is bought with power: for a fixed effect size a sequential test needs more samples than a correctly powered fixed-horizon test that is genuinely left alone until the end. The method assumes a single pre-declared metric and a stable randomisation unit, and it does not address multiple metrics or multiple variants.
records.counter_evidence: Kohavi, Deng and Vermeer treat peeking as a misunderstanding to be corrected rather than a workflow to be supported; the two positions differ on whether the operator or the statistic should change.

records.source: Kohavi, Deng and Vermeer, A/B Testing Intuition Busters: Common Misunderstandings in Online Controlled Experiments
records.study_design: Synthesis of practitioner errors with statistical argument, drawn from experimentation platforms at several large firms
records.population: Online controlled experiments at web-scale companies
records.finding: The dominant experimentation errors are interpretive, not computational: reading a p-value as the probability the result is chance, monitoring continuously with a fixed-horizon test (which can push the type I error rate far above the nominal five per cent), ignoring sample ratio mismatch, and forgetting that with roughly eighty-five to ninety per cent of ideas failing to move the target metric, the prior is against you and a bare significant result is more likely false than a naive reading suggests. Twyman's law follows: a surprisingly large effect is evidence of a bug before it is evidence of a win.
records.applicability_limits: Written from platforms running hundreds of concurrent experiments with millions of users; the low success base rate is measured on mature products where the obvious wins are gone, and an early-stage venture testing crude changes may face a different prior. It offers no method for a venture that cannot reach the sample size for a properly powered test at all.
records.counter_evidence: Its anti-peeking stance is answered by always-valid and group-sequential methods, which make monitoring legitimate rather than forbidden.

records.source: Kohavi, Deng, Frasca, Walker, Xu and Pohlmann, Online Controlled Experiments at Large Scale
records.study_design: Experience report on the Bing experimentation system
records.population: Over 200 concurrent experiments per day at Bing
records.licence: unknown (ACM proceedings; author copy served by exp-platform.com)
records.finding: At scale the binding constraint is trustworthiness, not throughput. Two mechanisms carry it: alerting rather than up-front testing, because the number of live variants makes exhaustive pre-release testing impossible, and explicit detection of interactions between concurrently running experiments. The report also defends deliberately running experiments expected to degrade the experience, on the grounds that the size of the loss is the only way to price the feature.
records.applicability_limits: Everything here presumes traffic that a small venture does not have; with one experiment at a time, interaction detection is moot and alerting has nothing to alert on. Thirteen years old, and the platform economics have changed.

records.source: Deng, Xu, Kohavi and Walker, Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data (CUPED)
records.study_design: Method with evaluation on Bing's production experimentation system
records.population: Bing online controlled experiments
records.licence: ACM copyright 2013, all rights reserved (stated on the paper); paraphrase only
records.finding: Sensitivity is cheaper to buy through variance reduction than through traffic. Using each user's pre-experiment behaviour as a covariate removes the part of the metric that has nothing to do with the treatment, and on Bing this cut variance by roughly half, which is the same power at half the users or half the duration. The precondition is that you already store per-unit history before the experiment starts.
records.applicability_limits: Requires a stable randomisation unit observed before the experiment, so it does nothing for new users, first-session funnels or anonymous traffic. Reported on one search product's metrics; the variance reduction achieved depends entirely on how strongly pre-period behaviour predicts in-period behaviour, and for rare conversion events that correlation can be near zero.

records.source: Fabijan, Gupchup, Gupta, Omhover, Qin, Vermeer and Dmitriev, Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments
records.study_design: Taxonomy derived from experiments across four companies and more than twenty-five products
records.population: Online controlled experiments serving hundreds of millions of users
records.finding: A mismatch between the assignment ratio you asked for and the ratio you observed invalidates the experiment outright, because whatever caused the imbalance almost certainly also biased the metric. The paper turns this into a diagnosis procedure by classifying causes into where they arise (assignment, execution, log processing, telemetry, interference), so the check is not just a red light but a search order.
records.applicability_limits: The chi-squared check needs enough units for the ratio deviation to be detectable, so small experiments can pass while badly broken. The taxonomy comes from large platforms with layered assignment services; a venture with one feature flag has fewer places for a mismatch to hide and a correspondingly shorter search.

records.source: spotify/confidence
records.finding: An open library that puts the corrections in the analysis path rather than in a checklist: z and Welch tests, group sequential testing, multiple-comparison correction, variance reduction and non-inferiority margins in one place. The existence of a maintained library at this size shows the statistical machinery is not a reason to buy a platform.
records.applicability_limits: Self-described beta with a small maintainer surface, and it analyses data you have already collected correctly; it cannot fix assignment, logging or sample ratio problems upstream. Choosing between its sequential and fixed-horizon paths is left to the user with no guidance on the power cost.

records.source: Snowplow Iglu schema registry
records.version_or_commit: unknown exact release; master branch inspected 2026-08-03
records.finding: Product analytics events are treated as versioned, resolvable schemas held in a registry, so an event is validated against a published contract at collection time and bad events are quarantined rather than silently landed. SchemaVer separates changes that break consumers from changes that only add, which makes the compatibility question explicit at the point of authoring.
records.applicability_limits: Registry, resolver and validation infrastructure is real operational weight, and it fits a pipeline you control end to end; a venture on a hosted analytics SDK cannot easily insert it. Validation checks structure, not whether the event fires at the right moment or means what the name says.
records.counter_evidence: The lighter convention-only approach (object-action naming plus a shared tracking plan) claims most of the benefit with none of the infrastructure, and no comparison of the two exists in the sources found.

records.source: Twilio Segment, Naming conventions for clean data
records.licence: Copyright Twilio Inc., all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: Event taxonomy is generated, not enumerated: pick the objects in the product and the actions that can be done to them, and every event name is an object-action pair. The corollary rule is that anything varying per occurrence belongs in a property, never in the event name, which is what stops an event catalogue exploding into thousands of near-duplicates.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor guidance whose enforcement story is that vendor's product, with no evidence beyond assertion. Casing conventions are arbitrary and only consistency matters. The page is silent on who owns the tracking plan and how a change to it is reviewed, which is the part that actually decays.

records.source: NIST SP 800-226, Guidelines for Evaluating Differential Privacy Guarantees
records.finding: A differential privacy claim is only meaningful with its parameters stated, and the guidance frames evaluation as a layered pyramid rather than a single epsilon number. It names privacy hazards, the gaps that open when the mathematics is realised in software, which is the honest way to read any vendor claim of privacy-preserving analytics: ask what the privacy unit is and what the implementation does that the proof does not cover.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance for evaluating differential privacy specifically; it does not tell you whether differential privacy is the right control for your case, and for a small venture the usual answer is that collecting less data is cheaper than noising it. Detail lives in the full document rather than the landing page inspected here.

records.source: Google differential-privacy libraries
records.version_or_commit: unknown exact release; main branch inspected 2026-08-03
records.finding: Working differentially private counts, sums, means, variances and quantiles with budget accounting are available as libraries, so the barrier to privacy-preserving aggregate reporting is design, not implementation. The documented limitation is the load-bearing part: the primitives assume each user contributes a bounded number of rows per partition and do not enforce that bound, so contribution limiting is the caller's job and getting it wrong silently voids the guarantee.
records.applicability_limits: Aggregate statistics only; nothing here helps with row-level data sharing or with re-identification risk in an event stream. Correct use requires choosing epsilon and the privacy unit, which the library cannot do for you. Maintainers commit to three months notice before dropping support, which is a short horizon for a dependency in a compliance path.

records.source: Diataxis documentation framework (site)
records.population: Technical documentation authors; originated in Django and Canonical practice
records.version_or_commit: diataxis.fr as published 2026-08-03; framework first released 2020 by Daniele Procida
records.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (stated in the diataxis-documentation-framework repository README)
records.finding: Documentation splits on two independent axes, action versus cognition and study versus work, giving four irreducible forms: tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation. The load-bearing claim is not the four boxes, it is that mixing forms inside one document is the dominant cause of documentation failure, because a reader in work mode cannot use a page that keeps stopping to teach. The framework is a diagnostic to apply to an existing page, not a folder layout to impose up front.
records.applicability_limits: Aimed at product documentation read by outsiders. It says nothing about internal engineering documentation whose main reader is the team that wrote it, nothing about machine readers, and offers no measurement of whether split documentation performs better. Adoption by Django, Canonical and Cloudflare is a popularity signal, not evidence of outcome.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0323 records the author's own concession that readers do not strictly separate these modes, and questions whether information architecture survives retrieval-mediated reading.
records.review: on-change-of:diataxis.fr revising the four-form model or the two axes

records.source: Tom Johnson, What is Diataxis and should you be using it with your documentation?
records.population: One experienced technical writer reflecting on the framework and on a conversation with its author
records.licence: unknown (no licence statement found on the page)
records.finding: Two reservations worth carrying: the four-form split has no research base beyond the author's practice and reads as an opinionated information model rather than a discovered one; and when a model rather than a navigation tree becomes the main way people reach documentation, the architecture matters less to the reader and more to whatever ingests the text. The author still keeps the framework as an analytical instrument, which is the honest position: use it to diagnose a bad page, do not defend it as measured.
records.applicability_limits: Single practitioner opinion, no data, and the retrieval argument was speculative when written. Useful as a named disagreement, not as evidence either way.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0322 holds that the forms follow from user needs rather than from taste.

records.source: DORA, Capabilities: Documentation quality
records.study_design: Cross-sectional self-report survey with latent-construct modelling; documentation quality measured by eight survey items covering clarity, findability and reliability
records.population: State of DevOps survey respondents, first measured in the 2021 cycle
records.version_or_commit: Capability page as published 2026-08-03, citing the 2021 Accelerate State of DevOps Report
records.finding: Documentation quality behaves as a multiplier on other capabilities rather than as a standalone practice: teams with above-average documentation get large reported lifts when they adopt trunk-based development, continuous integration, supply chain security, SRE and loose coupling, while teams with below-average documentation get small ones. The operational reading is that documenting a practice is part of adopting it, not a follow-up task, and that the measurable construct is clarity plus findability plus reliability, not page count.
records.applicability_limits: Self-reported, cross-sectional and correlational. Documentation quality and capability adoption are both reported by the same respondent, so common-method bias is unaddressed and the direction of the arrow is not established: mature teams plausibly write better documentation because they are mature. The published lift percentages are large enough to warrant suspicion of the modelling, and the capability page states no causal caveat of its own. The eight items are not reproduced on the page, so the construct cannot be reused verbatim.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0336 argues single productivity numbers built from mixed self-report and system data mislead when used as targets.
records.review: on-change-of:a DORA cycle re-measuring documentation quality

records.source: Aghajani, Nagy, Vega-Marquez, Linares-Vasquez, Moreno, Bavota, Lanza, Software Documentation Issues Unveiled
records.study_design: Mining study: 878 documentation-related artefacts from four sources (GitHub issues, pull requests, mailing lists, Stack Overflow), manually analysed and coded into a taxonomy
records.population: Open-source projects and their documentation discussions
records.licence: unknown (IEEE/ACM proceedings copyright; no open-access copy verified)
records.finding: A taxonomy of documentation defects built from what people actually complained about, not from what they say in surveys. The value for a rule set is that documentation failure is decomposable into named, detectable categories (information content, completeness, correctness, consistency, process, tooling) rather than being a single quality vibe, which is the precondition for putting any of it under an automated check.
records.applicability_limits: Open-source artefacts only, pre-2019, so nothing about internal engineering documentation or machine-consumed documentation. The taxonomy counts complaints, which over-samples defects people bother to report and under-samples documentation so bad nobody engages with it. I verified design and sample size from the conference record and abstract, not from the full text.

records.source: Aghajani, Nagy, Linares-Vasquez, Moreno, Bavota, Lanza, Shepherd, Software Documentation: The Practitioners' Perspective
records.study_design: Two surveys of 146 practitioners in total, rating perceived relevance and frequency of documentation issues and the documentation types used per task
records.population: Software practitioners, industry and open source
records.licence: unknown (ACM Digital Library; the ACM landing page returned 403 to automated fetch)
records.finding: What practitioners rate as most damaging is absence, not prose quality: missing installation, deployment and release instructions (68 per cent), missing user documentation (65 per cent) and missing developer guidelines (60 per cent) were both important and frequently met. Correctness and completeness dominate style. That ranks the work: a terse, correct, present runbook beats a polished, incomplete guide.
records.applicability_limits: Perception data, self-reported relevance rather than measured cost, sample of 146 across two surveys, and pre-agentic. The percentages are the share rating an issue important, not a defect rate. Full text was not retrievable through the ACM landing page, so figures come from the published abstract and secondary reporting.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0322 and the style-guide sources treat form and consistency as load-bearing; this source says form is second order behind existence and accuracy.

records.source: Barik, Smith, Lubick, Holmes, Feng, Murphy-Hill, Parnin, Do Developers Read Compiler Error Messages?
records.study_design: Eye-tracking experiment, 56 participants resolving planted Java defects in Eclipse, with reading-difficulty measures regressed against task performance
records.population: Undergraduate and graduate software engineering students
records.licence: unknown (author-hosted preprint; ICSE 2017 proceedings copyright applies to the published version)
records.finding: Error messages are documentation with the highest read rate in the system. Participants did read them, spent 13 to 25 per cent of total task time doing so, found them about as hard to read as source code, and reading difficulty significantly predicted how long the fix took. So message wording is not cosmetic: it is on the critical path of every failure, and it is the one page nobody has to be persuaded to open.
records.applicability_limits: Students, one language, one IDE, planted defects, 2017 tooling and no LLM in the loop. The direction of the finding is robust; the percentages are not a target. Nothing here tests whether the same holds when the reader is an agent parsing the message.

records.source: Rust Compiler Development Guide, Errors and lints (diagnostic style)
records.population: rustc contributors writing compiler diagnostics
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 (stated by the guide); rustc code is MIT or Apache-2.0
records.finding: A working, enforceable error-message contract exists and can be copied as decision rules rather than prose. Structure: level, stable error code, one general primary message, a window showing the offending span, sub-diagnostics for detail, and long-form explanation behind an explicit --explain rather than inline. Wording: lower case, no trailing punctuation, plain English, identifiers in backticks, prefer specific words over 'illegal'. Most transferable of all, suggestions carry a declared confidence level (machine-applicable, has-placeholders, maybe-incorrect, unspecified), so a downstream tool can decide whether to auto-apply. That last idea is directly reusable for agent-facing errors.
records.applicability_limits: A compiler with an error-code registry and a span model. Applications without stable identifiers for failures cannot mint error codes cheaply. The four-tier applicability scale presumes something can act on the suggestion automatically; where no fixer exists the tier is decoration.

records.source: Prana, Treude, Thung, Atapattu, Lo, Categorizing the Content of GitHub README Files
records.study_design: Manual annotation of 4,226 README sections from 393 randomly sampled GitHub repositories, followed by a supervised multi-label classifier evaluated at F1 0.746
records.population: Random sample of GitHub repositories
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:1802.06997; published in Empirical Software Engineering 2019, doi 10.1007/s10664-018-9660-3
records.licence: unknown (arXiv preprint; check the arXiv licence line before reuse. Springer holds the journal version)
records.finding: READMEs cluster on What and How and systematically omit Why and status. The named gap is the decision-relevant part: a reader cannot tell whether a project is maintained, what it is for, or whether they should use it, which are precisely the questions that cost the most to answer any other way. A README section taxonomy (What, Why, How, When, Who, References, Contribution) is concrete enough to check mechanically for presence.
records.applicability_limits: Descriptive of open-source READMEs sampled before 2018. It measures what is present, not what readers needed, and does not link section presence to any outcome. Internal repositories with a different reader model are out of scope.

records.source: rustdoc book, Documentation tests
records.population: Rust crate authors
records.version_or_commit: The rustdoc book as published 2026-08-03, covering the 2024 edition merged-doctest behaviour
records.licence: MIT or Apache-2.0 (Rust project dual licence)
records.finding: The strongest available answer to documentation drift is to make the example the test. Every fenced example in a doc comment is compiled and run; it passes if it compiles and does not panic. The design detail that makes it usable is the escape hatches: hidden setup lines so the printed example stays minimal while still compiling, and explicit no_run, ignore, should_panic and compile_fail markers so an example that cannot be executed has to declare why. Absence of that declaration is itself a check.
records.applicability_limits: Requires a language and toolchain with first-class doctest support. Doctests only prove the snippet compiles and does not panic, not that it is the right thing to show, and merged doctests in the 2024 edition change isolation assumptions. Prose around the example remains unverified.

records.source: lychee link checker
records.population: Documentation and static-site repositories using CI
records.version_or_commit: master branch, approximately 2,132 commits and 3.8k stars at access; latest tagged release not verified from the repository page
records.licence: Apache-2.0 or MIT (dual, stated in the README)
records.finding: Link rot is mechanically checkable and the tool exposes exactly the knobs needed to make the check binding rather than noisy: distinct exit codes (0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 link failure, 3 config error) so the pipeline can tell a broken link from a broken checker, fragment and anchor validation rather than URL-only checking, on-disk caching with a max age, and file-based exclusions. Anchor checking is the part that matters most internally, because internal cross-references break silently on a heading rename.
records.applicability_limits: External link checking is inherently flaky against rate limits and transient outages, so making it blocking on external URLs buys false failures. The defensible split is blocking on internal links and anchors, advisory on external. Verifies reachability only, never that the link points somewhere still relevant.

records.source: GitLab, Documentation testing
records.population: GitLab's own documentation suite across five repositories
records.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (stated in the site footer)
records.finding: A worked example of docs-as-code where the gate is real and graded. Blocking: markdownlint structure, Vale content rules, internal link and anchor validation across sibling repositories, Mermaid syntax, redirect verification when a page is deleted or renamed, verification that generated reference (GraphQL) was regenerated rather than hand-edited, and a partial site build. Advisory and explicitly non-blocking: translated-content link checks. Vale findings are surfaced as code-quality annotations inside the merge request diff rather than only in a log, which is the difference between a check people act on and one they scroll past.
records.applicability_limits: Scaled to a dedicated technical-writing function, a Hugo site and a large CI budget. The transferable parts are cheap (link and anchor checking, redirect-on-rename, regenerated-file verification); the site build and the translation pipeline are not. Being an exemplar it shows what one organisation chose, with no evidence that the chosen split is optimal.

records.source: Keep a Changelog
records.population: Projects publishing release notes to human consumers
records.finding: A changelog is a curated, human-addressed artefact and the specification is explicit that generating it from commit diffs fails, because the log is full of merges and internal churn that no consumer can act on. The usable rules: one entry per version, newest first, dated, grouped into a fixed six-way vocabulary (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security), an Unreleased section maintained continuously so the release is a rename rather than an archaeology exercise, and deprecations announced before removal.
records.applicability_limits: Written for libraries with external consumers. An internal service whose only consumers are two other services of the same estate gets less from a prose changelog than from a machine-readable compatibility diff. Version 1.1.0 has been static since 2019, so it does not address monorepos, per-package changesets, or agent-authored entries. It also sits in tension with commit-derived automation, which is what most estates actually run.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0170 (Conventional Commits) makes changelog generation a derivation from commit history, the exact automation this specification cautions against. The reconciliation is that Conventional Commits constrains the log at write time so the derivation is not noise, but the disagreement about who curates is real.
records.review: on-change-of:a Keep a Changelog release beyond 1.1.0

records.source: Google developer documentation style guide, Highlights
records.population: Developer-facing documentation authors
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for content; Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Most house style is arbitrary but a small subset is mechanically checkable and worth binding: second person, active voice, present tense, sentence case for headings, code font for code-related text, numbered lists for sequences, serial commas, unambiguous date formats, alt text on images. The principle to take is the split itself, a short executable subset that a linter enforces and everything else left to the author, rather than a long guide nobody reads.
records.applicability_limits: Google's conventions, not universal truth, and written for American English. This repository's voice law already contradicts parts of it. Adopt the enforceable-subset principle and the specific mechanical rules that survive a British-English house voice; do not adopt the guide wholesale.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0326 finds practitioners rank missing content far above style, so style enforcement that displaces coverage work is a net loss.

records.source: Vale prose linter
records.population: Documentation repositories enforcing a style guide in CI
records.version_or_commit: v3 branch, approximately 1,982 commits at access; latest tagged release not verified from the repository page
records.finding: Prose style becomes governance only when it is executable, the same move EV-0137 makes for API conventions. Vale applies rule packages to Markdown, AsciiDoc, reStructuredText, HTML and XML and is the standard mechanism behind GitLab's blocking content check. The design point worth copying is severity levels, so a house rule can ship as a suggestion, be observed, and only then be promoted to an error.
records.applicability_limits: Regex and word-list rules catch banned terms, passive voice and heading case; they cannot judge whether a page is correct, complete or well organised, which is where the measured cost lies. Exit-code and minAlertLevel behaviour was not verifiable from the repository landing page and must be confirmed against the current release before it is made blocking.
records.review: on-change-of:a Vale major release changing rule or severity semantics

records.source: DX, Measuring developer productivity with the DX Core 4
records.study_design: Vendor framework paper combining self-report survey instruments with system telemetry; reported aggregate outcomes from customer deployments, no control group
records.population: Engineering organisations using the vendor's platform
records.licence: unknown (copyright DX 2026; no reuse licence stated)
records.finding: Four dimensions (speed, effectiveness, quality, business impact) unifying DORA, SPACE and DevEx. The reusable caution, stated by the vendor against its own interest, is that throughput measures are signal only when counterbalanced by an opposing measure, never turned into a target or reward, and communicated carefully. Notably the framework does not carry onboarding time as a headline measure.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor-authored, commercially motivated, no control group, and the reported efficiency gains are customer aggregates rather than a study. Self-report items are acknowledged as less precise than system data. Nothing here is usable as an effect size; the Goodhart caution is the transferable part.

records.source: SPDX License List
records.licence: unknown (no reuse licence stated on the list landing page; Linux Foundation site terms of use apply)
records.finding: Licence identity is a stable short string, not prose: every listed licence and exception has a short identifier, a full name, canonical licence text and a permanent URL, identifiers are never repurposed and are deprecated instead, and the list stays deliberately neutral by recording OSI approval and FSF free status as two separate flag columns rather than one verdict. The operational rule is that a dependency record carries an identifier, and any judgement about that identifier is made once, centrally, against the identifier.
records.applicability_limits: A naming registry only. It confers no permission, states no obligations, ranks nothing and says nothing about whether a combination is lawful; it also cannot describe a licence that is not on the list except through a LicenseRef.
records.counter_evidence: The deliberate neutrality means the list will happily give an identifier to a licence that is neither open source nor safe to depend on, so an allowlist keyed on identifiers still needs a separate policy layer.

records.source: SPDX Specification, licence expressions annex
records.licence: Community Specification License 1.0 and CC BY 3.0 Unported
records.finding: Real licensing is compound and the grammar says so: AND means every listed licence must be complied with at once, OR means the recipient chooses one, WITH attaches a named exception, the plus suffix means that version or later, LicenseRef covers anything off the list, and precedence runs plus, WITH, AND, OR with parentheses overriding. The decision rule this yields is that an OR expression is a choice a project must actually record having made, and an AND expression is a set of obligations that all bite.
records.applicability_limits: Syntax, not semantics. The grammar cannot tell you whether an AND combination is lawful, and a tool that emits a well-formed expression has still only reported what a file claims about itself.
records.counter_evidence: The annex read here does not cover NOASSERTION and NONE, which is where most real scan output lands, so the tidy grammar understates how much of a dependency tree resolves to nothing usable.

records.source: Open Source Initiative, The Open Source Definition
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 (site content, attribution to Opensource.org)
records.finding: The ten criteria define open source by what a licence may not restrict rather than by what it must require: no restriction on redistribution or sale, source in preferred form, derived works permitted under the same terms, no discrimination against persons or fields of endeavour, rights travelling automatically with the code, and no product, technology or interface specificity. A licence that limits the field of use, however reasonable the limit sounds, is not open source under this definition and the venture should treat it as proprietary.
records.applicability_limits: A definition of licence eligibility, not a compatibility rule and not a risk rating. It has been stable since 2007 and says nothing about source-available, ethical-source or business-source licences that have appeared since.
records.counter_evidence: OSI approval and safety are different axes: a licence can satisfy all ten criteria and still be drafted badly enough that Blue Oak rates it lead, and conversely a non-approved licence may be trivially safe to use.

records.source: Free Software Foundation, License Compatibility and Relicensing
records.licence: CC BY-ND 4.0 (no derivatives, so paraphrase the principle and never adapt the text)
records.finding: Compatibility means you can merge the code and still comply with every licence at once, and it is directional: lax licences absorb into anything, copyleft licences are unavoidably incompatible with each other unless one of them carries an explicit compatibility provision. Two named consequences that a routing rule must encode are that GPLv2 and GPLv3 do not combine, and that the Apache 2.0 patent terms are incompatible with GPLv2 while GPLv3 was written to accept them.
records.applicability_limits: The position of one advocacy organisation, stated as doctrine rather than tested in court, and it addresses combination of source into one program. It does not settle where a program boundary lies for a service, a container image or a plug-in.
records.counter_evidence: The FSF frames the same facts as an argument for choosing GPLv3-or-later, whereas the ASF policy reads the identical incompatibility as a reason to exclude the GPL family entirely; the facts agree and the recommended action does not.

records.source: GNU Affero General Public License version 3, OSI-hosted text
records.version_or_commit: AGPL-3.0, approved 2008-03-03; page licence per opensource.org footer
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the OSI page; the licence text itself is copyright FSF, verbatim copying permitted, modification not permitted
records.finding: Section 13 moves the trigger from distribution to interaction: a modified version that users reach remotely over a network must offer those users the corresponding source of that version from a network server at no charge, and the licence explicitly permits combination with GPLv3 work with each part keeping its own terms. For a venture whose product is a hosted service this is the one copyleft term that bites without anything ever being shipped, so AGPL dependencies need a decision before they enter, not at release.
records.applicability_limits: The obligation attaches to a modified version made available to remote users; the licence text alone does not resolve what counts as modification, what counts as the same program when the AGPL code sits behind an internal service boundary, or how the offer must be surfaced.
records.counter_evidence: Read narrowly, an unmodified AGPL component run as a back end triggers nothing extra, which is why some teams treat AGPL as usable and others ban it outright; the disagreement is about the modification boundary, not about the text.

records.source: Apache Software Foundation, ASF third-party licence policy
records.version_or_commit: unknown (no revision or last-modified date shown on the page)
records.finding: The reusable shape is a standing three-bucket verdict decided once by people and then applied mechanically by everyone else: category A may be included freely with attribution, category B may be included in binary form only in convenience distributions and never in a source release, and category X may not be distributed at all. GPL and AGPL sit in X because they impose terms on the larger work, weak copyleft such as MPL, EPL and CDDL sits in B, and one narrow exception, GPLv2 with the Classpath exception, is carved out explicitly rather than by case-by-case judgement.
records.applicability_limits: This is a policy tuned to one distributor's promise, that everything it releases stays permissively licensed. It reasons about source and binary releases, so it does not directly answer questions about a hosted service, an internal tool or a build-time-only dependency.
records.counter_evidence: The blanket exclusion of GPL is stricter than the law requires for a venture that never distributes the combined work, so copying the categories without copying the reason produces a rule that blocks safe dependencies while saying nothing about the network trigger that actually matters.

records.source: Blue Oak Council Permissive License List
records.licence: unknown (no reuse licence stated on the list page; the list is also published as JSON and as an npm package)
records.finding: Permissive is not one bucket, it is a quality gradient, and the gradient is publishable as machine-readable data: gold for licences that address patents explicitly, use robust drafting and ask only for simple notice, silver for strong drafting missing patent terms or asking more than notice, bronze for missing but non-essential elements or awkward extra restrictions, lead for missing essential elements or burdensome and informally worded terms. The rule this supports is that the rating is a tiebreak for choosing an outbound licence and for triaging inbound risk, never a permission.
records.applicability_limits: The ratings are the collective judgement of the council's lawyers, not a measurement or a legal opinion for any specific use, and the list covers permissive licences only, so it is silent on every copyleft question.
records.counter_evidence: A licence can be OSI approved and rated lead, so this axis and the Open Source Definition axis will sometimes point in opposite directions for the same licence.

records.source: REUSE Specification, Free Software Foundation Europe
records.finding: Licensing becomes checkable when it is declared per file rather than inferred per repository: every covered file carries SPDX-FileCopyrightText and SPDX-License-Identifier in a comment header, files that cannot carry comments get a sibling .license file, every licence referenced has its full text in LICENSES/ named by SPDX identifier, and bulk cases are declared in REUSE.toml by glob with defined precedence. A lint tool then turns the whole question into a pass or fail in CI, which is what makes it enforceable by a cold agent.
records.applicability_limits: It proves declarations are present and internally consistent, nothing more. A conformant repository can still declare the wrong licence, and the specification says nothing about whether the declared combination is compatible.
records.counter_evidence: The per-file discipline is real overhead on small repositories, and repository-level detection tools deliberately guess instead, which is why most projects in the wild are not conformant.

records.source: Developer Certificate of Origin
records.licence: copyright the Linux Foundation and its contributors; verbatim copying and distribution permitted, modification not permitted
records.finding: Inbound contribution rights can be handled by certification rather than by contract: the contributor asserts that they wrote the change and may submit it, or that it derives from work they are entitled to submit under a compatible open source licence, or that someone who so certified passed it to them unmodified, and they accept that the record is public and permanent. The obligation is discharged by one sign-off line per commit, which a hook can check, so the process cost is near zero and the evidence is in the history.
records.applicability_limits: The DCO is an assertion by the contributor, not a grant of rights to the project, and it presumes the project already has an inbound licence that the contribution comes under. It gives no patent grant and no warranty, and it does not help with contributions of code the contributor was wrong about.
records.counter_evidence: Projects that need to relicense later, or that want explicit patent and moral-rights positions, use a contributor licence agreement instead; no source read at this cutoff compares the two on outcomes, so the choice rests on assertion rather than evidence.

records.source: ScanCode Toolkit
records.licence: Apache-2.0 for the code, CC-BY-4.0 for the reference licence datasets, bundled third-party components under their own terms including LGPL and GPL
records.finding: Licence detection works by full text comparison against a curated database of licence texts rather than by regular-expression matching on headers, and it scans copyrights, package manifests and declared dependencies in the same pass, which is what lets a build emit an inventory instead of a guess. The practical rule is that the scanner produces the inventory and a human produces the verdict.
records.applicability_limits: The project claims the most accurate detection engine but publishes no accuracy figure on the page read here, and no statement was found disclaiming legal advice, so the accuracy claim is a vendor claim. Detection also cannot see licence terms that exist only in a separate agreement or in a file the scan does not cover.
records.counter_evidence: Repository-level detectors used by hosting platforms disagree with file-level scans routinely, and a scan of a project that follows REUSE is answering a much easier question than a scan of one that does not, so measured accuracy is not portable between codebases.

records.source: OpenChain ISO/IEC 5230 licence compliance standard
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the specification documents, CC0 for the reference material
records.finding: The standard certifies a process, not an artefact, and it is deliberately minimal: name the places in the lifecycle where compliance decisions happen, assign the roles and responsibilities that make those decisions, and show the arrangement is sustainable rather than a one-off audit. Conformance can be self-declared against a published checklist or attested by a third party, and the two routes are treated as the same standard rather than two tiers of truth.
records.applicability_limits: Written for organisations with staff to assign roles to; a one-person venture can satisfy the letter trivially and learn nothing. It says nothing about which licences to accept and nothing about how to resolve a specific compatibility question.
records.counter_evidence: Self-certification against your own checklist is exactly the failure mode a standard is supposed to prevent, and no source read here measures whether conformant organisations have fewer licence incidents.

records.source: choosealicense.com, No License
records.version_or_commit: unknown (no version or revision date shown; GitHub-maintained site)
records.finding: Absence of a licence is not permission, it is exclusive copyright by default, and platform mechanics do not change that: hosting terms may let anyone view and fork a public repository while granting no right to use, modify or redistribute the code. The only routes out are to ask the owner to add a licence, to find an alternative, or to negotiate a private licence, so an unlicensed dependency is a blocking finding rather than an unknown to be filled in later.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance written by a hosting platform for the general case, not legal advice and not jurisdiction-specific; it also addresses public repositories on that platform and does not cover code received privately or under a separate agreement.

records.source: UK GDPR Article 13, information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject
records.version_or_commit: revised text showing amendments up to 2026-08-02, including Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 changes in force from 2026-02-05
records.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0, with material reused from EUR-Lex under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU
records.finding: A privacy notice is a fixed checklist due at the moment of collection, not a document written when convenient: controller identity and contact, any data protection officer, purposes and lawful basis, the legitimate interests relied on where that is the basis, categories of recipient, third-country transfers and safeguards, retention period or the criteria for it, the access, rectification, erasure and restriction rights, withdrawal of consent, and the automated decision-making position. The revised UK text now also names two distinct complaint routes that must be told to the subject, to the controller under section 164A and to the Commissioner under section 165.
records.applicability_limits: Statutory duty in the UK only, and it states what must be said, not how to say it, at what reading level or in what format. It is silent on the harder questions of whether the chosen lawful basis is correct and whether the processing itself is fair.

records.source: The Data Protection (Charges and Information) Regulations 2018
records.version_or_commit: SI 2018 No. 480, original text as made
records.finding: There is a statutory duty on data controllers to pay a charge to the Information Commissioner and to supply information, with the amount set by regulation, special handling for partnerships and for school governing bodies, and a schedule of exempt processing. For a venture the routing consequence is binary and cheap to check: before any personal data is processed, run the registration self-assessment and either pay or record which schedule exemption applies, because this is a duty that exists independently of how good the privacy notice is.
records.applicability_limits: The version read is the text as originally made, so the tier amounts stated in it may have been uprated since and must be checked against the current fee before relying on a number. Only the table of contents and structure were retrieved at this access, not the tier figures.

records.source: European Commission, summary of the Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)
records.version_or_commit: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847; entry into force 2024-12-10, conformity assessment bodies from 2026-06-11, reporting obligations from 2026-09-11, full application from 2027-12-11
records.licence: unknown (no reuse notice shown on the page; Commission Decision 2011/833/EU typically applies to Commission documents)
records.finding: The regulator's line is drawn at commercial activity, not at price: free and open-source software published outside a commercial activity is out of scope, but the same software made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity is in, and a manufacturer is anyone who markets a product with digital elements under their own name whether paid, monetised or free. A separate lighter category, the open-source software steward, carries a duty to keep a documented cybersecurity policy and to handle vulnerability reports but attracts no penalties.
records.applicability_limits: EU market scope, so it reaches a UK venture only through what it places on that market, and this is the Commission's own summary rather than the operative text of the Regulation, which was not retrieved at this access. It sets obligations without telling a very small manufacturer what proportionate evidence looks like.
records.counter_evidence: The boundary between publishing open source and making it available in the course of a commercial activity is the contested part, and the summary asserts the line without resolving the cases that matter, such as a maintainer with sponsorship or a hosted version of their own project.

records.source: United States Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence report
records.version_or_commit: Part 1 Digital Replicas 2024-07-31 final; Part 2 Copyrightability 2025-01-29 final; Part 3 Generative AI Training 2025-05-09 pre-publication, final version expected without substantive change
records.finding: The question of who owns machine-generated output is being answered by a national copyright authority in staged public reports rather than settled, and the staging itself is the signal: copyrightability and training data are separate inquiries with separate conclusions. A venture shipping agent-written code should therefore treat authorship and provenance as an open position to record, not a solved one to assume.
records.applicability_limits: United States law and the position of one office, not binding in the UK and not a court ruling. The hub page read here does not state the Office's conclusions on the human-contribution threshold, so no threshold should be quoted from this record; the underlying part reports were not read at this cutoff.
records.counter_evidence: No equivalent UK determination was located at this cutoff, so the UK position on agent-written code is genuinely unresolved rather than merely unread.

records.source: Google Search Central, SEO Starter Guide
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: The search engine itself names most of the folk SEO surface as inert: keywords meta tag unused, no word-count target, heading order irrelevant to ranking, keywords in the domain or URL near worthless, and E-E-A-T explicitly not a ranking factor. What it does claim to weigh is content people find useful, crawlability and discovery through links. The decision rule that follows is to spend the budget on the small set of things the operator of the index says it reads, and to treat every other lever as a preference an agent must not assert as law.
records.applicability_limits: One vendor describing its own closed ranking system with no external verification, and the doc gives no weights or thresholds, so it settles what is not worth doing far better than it settles what is. Says nothing about Bing, AI assistants that do not use Google's index, or any non-search channel.
records.counter_evidence: The SEO trade press routinely reports ranking correlations that contradict Google's public denials; none of that reporting is a controlled experiment either, so the disagreement is unresolved rather than settled in Google's favour.
records.review: on-change-of:Google Search Central SEO Starter Guide revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Spam policies for Google web search
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Sixteen named policies, of which three bite directly on agent-assisted marketing: scaled content abuse (many pages generated mainly to move rankings rather than help a reader), site reputation abuse (renting an established domain's ranking signals to third-party content) and expired domain abuse. The policy hinges on purpose rather than production method, so the binding rule for an agent estate is a per-page purpose test and a human-attributable owner, not a cap on how much the machine writes.
records.applicability_limits: Enforcement is discretionary and opaque, with no published detection thresholds, so the policy states a boundary without letting anyone measure their distance from it. Written for web search, not for AI answer surfaces or other engines.
records.review: on-change-of:Google Search spam policies revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, General structured data guidelines
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Markup must describe what a reader can actually see on the page, marked-up pages must not be blocked from the crawler, and the penalty for breach is loss of rich-result eligibility rather than a ranking drop. That gives a clean machine-checkable contract: every marked-up property has a visible counterpart in the rendered DOM, and the blast radius of getting it wrong is bounded and known in advance.
records.applicability_limits: Governs eligibility for Google's rich results only. Says nothing about whether any rich result is worth having, and the required and recommended property sets differ per feature type, so a generic validator is not enough.
records.review: on-change-of:Google general structured data guidelines revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: The guidance is a self-assessment questionnaire organised as who wrote it, how it was made and why it exists, and it asks that substantial automation including AI generation be self-evident to the visitor. It does not ban machine-written content; it asks for disclosed provenance and a purpose other than ranking. For an agent estate that converts neatly into a per-artefact provenance record.
records.applicability_limits: A questionnaire, not a scoring rubric: two honest people can answer the same way about pages of very different quality, and none of it is externally auditable. The stricter Your Money or Your Life framing is asserted without published criteria.
records.review: on-change-of:Google helpful content guidance revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Optimising your website for AI features on Google Search
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Google states there are no additional requirements or special optimisations for AI Overviews and AI Mode, and specifically that no new machine-readable file, AI text file or markup is needed. Eligibility is ordinary indexing plus snippet eligibility. The binding consequence is that a pack must not let an agent invent a generative-engine-optimisation workstream on the strength of vendor-adjacent hype.
records.applicability_limits: Covers Google's surfaces only. Other assistants crawl and cite differently, and some publishers do serve llms.txt for non-Google consumers, so the claim is narrow rather than universal. Google has a commercial interest in discouraging parallel optimisation channels, so this is a self-interested denial, not neutral evidence.
records.counter_evidence: The llms.txt proposal and its adopters constitute a live counter-practice, unvalidated by any measurement this research could find.
records.review: on-change-of:Google AI features guidance revision date

records.source: RFC 9309, Robots Exclusion Protocol
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style licence on code components); text reproducible under RFC terms
records.finding: Crawler access rules are advisory only: the RFC states plainly that the protocol is not a substitute for content security measures. It also fixes the failure semantics that matter operationally, a 5xx on robots.txt means the crawler must assume complete disallow, and cached rules should not be used beyond twenty four hours. So a botched robots.txt deploy is a self-inflicted deindexing incident, which makes robots.txt a release-gated artefact rather than a marketing file.
records.applicability_limits: Compliance is voluntary; hostile scrapers ignore it entirely. The RFC governs crawling, not indexing, so a disallowed URL can still surface from external links.

records.source: RFC 8058, Signalling One-Click Functionality for List Email Headers
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style licence on code components); text reproducible under RFC terms
records.finding: One-click unsubscribe is a hard technical contract, not a courtesy: an HTTPS List-Unsubscribe URI plus List-Unsubscribe-Post, both covered by the DKIM signature, recipient and list identity encoded in the URI, no cookies or HTTP authorisation, and no confirmation page. The URI should carry an opaque hard-to-forge component that the server validates, which is what stops the unsubscribe endpoint becoming an open denial-of-subscription hole.
records.applicability_limits: Specifies the signalling mechanism only. It does not say how fast the suppression must take effect, does not cover consent capture, and does not reach any channel other than mail.

records.source: Google Workspace Admin Help, Email sender guidelines
records.version_or_commit: requirements effective 2024-02-01, page as accessed 2026-08-03; no explicit revision id published
records.finding: Deliverability has a published numeric gate. Every sender needs SPF or DKIM, valid forward and reverse DNS, TLS, RFC 5322 conformance and a Postmaster Tools spam rate under 0.30 per cent. Bulk senders above five thousand messages a day additionally need SPF and DKIM and DMARC, From-header alignment with the SPF or DKIM domain, and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe with a visible in-body link. That converts a soft craft into a preflight checklist a machine can assert before a first send.
records.applicability_limits: Gmail's rules for Gmail. Yahoo and Microsoft publish overlapping but not identical thresholds, and reporting at this cutoff says Yahoo computes the spam-rate denominator differently, from inbox-delivered mail rather than all delivered mail, so a single number cannot be treated as universal. The spam-rate figure is only observable through Google's own Postmaster Tools, which requires DKIM-signed volume to populate.
records.licence_evidence: "Email sender guidelines - Gmail Help" states no content licence. Footer carries only "©2026 Google" and links to Privacy Policy, Terms of Service and Program Policies. No Creative Commons or other licence designation appears.

records.source: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003, regulation 22
records.version_or_commit: SI 2003/2426 reg 22, as amended; text showing amendments in force to 2026-02-05 including the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 charity exception at paragraph 3A
records.finding: Unsolicited marketing mail to an individual subscriber requires prior consent, with one narrow escape: the soft opt-in, which needs all three of contact details obtained in the course of a sale or sales negotiation with that person, marketing of similar products and services only, and a simple free refusal route offered both at collection and in every subsequent message. The provenance of every address is therefore a compliance fact that must be stored with the address, not inferred later.
records.applicability_limits: UK law, and the regulation covers electronic mail to subscribers; the individual versus corporate subscriber distinction and the enforcement practice sit in ICO guidance rather than in the regulation text. EU member states implement the parent directive with local variation, and US CAN-SPAM is an opt-out regime entirely, so a single global consent rule is wrong in one direction or the other.

records.source: Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Bhargava and Chapsky, A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
records.study_design: Fifteen large-scale randomised advertising experiments used as ground truth, against which several observational estimators (exposed versus unexposed comparison, regression, propensity and matching methods) are re-estimated on the same data
records.population: Facebook advertisers in the United States; approximately 500 million user-experiment observations and 1.6 billion ad impressions
records.version_or_commit: Marketing Science vol 38 no 2, pages 193 to 225, published March 2019
records.licence: unknown (INFORMS subscription content; abstract publicly readable)
records.finding: With individual-level data far richer than any small venture will ever hold, observational estimates of advertising effect still failed to reproduce the randomised estimates, even after conditioning on extensive demographic and behavioural variables. The authors conclude the industry's usual data does not contain the exogenous variation needed. The decision rule is that any causal claim about a channel must come from a randomised holdout, and dashboard attribution is at best a bookkeeping convention.
records.applicability_limits: One platform, one era, mostly large advertisers with big budgets and small percentage effects; it does not follow that observational methods fail equally in every setting, and the paper does not tell a two-person venture what to do when a holdout is unaffordable. Access here was the public abstract and record page rather than the full text.
records.counter_evidence: Later work in the same journal, Close Enough? (Marketing Science 2023), explores non-experimental approaches more sympathetically, so the field's position is a spectrum rather than a flat prohibition.

records.source: Lewis, Zettelmeyer, Gordon et al, Amazon Ads Multi-Touch Attribution
records.study_design: Methodology paper describing an attribution system that calibrates machine-learned observational credit allocation against randomised controlled trials
records.population: Amazon Ads advertisers and shoppers
records.finding: The stated trade-off is explicit: observational models scale and are precise but can be biased, randomised trials are unbiased but noisy, so credit allocation is anchored to experimental estimates and the model only distributes within that anchor. The transferable rule is that an attribution model is a way of spreading an experimentally measured total, never a way of producing one.
records.applicability_limits: A preprint by the platform about its own product, not independently replicated, and it needs a continuous RCT programme at a scale no small venture has. It is evidence for the architecture of the argument rather than for the numbers.
records.review: on-change-of:arXiv 2508.08209 new version or journal publication

records.source: Google Analytics Help, Attribution and attribution modelling in Google Analytics 4
records.version_or_commit: page as accessed 2026-08-03; documents the November 2023 model removal
records.finding: The dominant analytics vendor deleted first-click, linear, time-decay and position-based attribution from its own product in November 2023, leaving data-driven attribution and two last-click variants, and it excludes direct visits from credit unless the whole path is direct. That is a vendor conceding that heuristic credit-splitting rules were arbitrary. A pack should therefore treat any percentage split across touchpoints as a reporting convention to be declared, never as a measured quantity.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation of a proprietary model whose internals are not published and cannot be audited or reproduced. Coverage degrades where consent is refused or cross-device identity is unavailable, and the doc does not quantify that gap.
records.licence_evidence: "Get started with attribution - Analytics Help" states no content licence. The footer links only to Google's general Privacy Policy and Terms of Service, which are not a licence declaration for the page content.

records.source: Reforge, Growth Loops are the New Funnels (Balfour, Winters, Kwok, Chen)
records.version_or_commit: unknown; essay series first circulated July 2018, no revision id published
records.finding: The argued case against funnels is organisational as much as mathematical: a funnel splits strategy and ownership by stage, so marketing optimises acquisition and product optimises retention against each other, and growth stays linear because output never re-enters input. A loop is a closed system whose output is reinvested as input. The usable rule is to require a named reinvestment step in any growth plan, and to treat a plan with no reinvestment step as a paid-acquisition budget rather than a growth strategy.
records.applicability_limits: Practitioner essay with no data, no measurement and no falsifiable claim; a consultancy's positioning artefact for its own curriculum. Direct access was refused with HTTP 403 at this cutoff, so the content here rests on the authors' own public thread and secondary summaries rather than the page itself, and the argument should be marked down accordingly.
records.counter_evidence: Nothing in the loop argument is inconsistent with funnel analytics as a diagnostic; the essay overstates the opposition, and tools such as PostHog (EV-0367) continue to ship funnels because step-level drop-off is still the cheapest diagnostic available.
records.review: on-change-of:direct access to the Reforge essay becoming possible
records.licence_evidence: "Growth Loops are the New Funnels | Reforge Blog" states no licence. A full-text scan of the rendered page for "licence/license/Creative Commons/copyright/rights reserved" matched only the footer navigation link labels "Terms of Service", "Copyright Policy", "Privacy Policy", "Cookies Policy" - link names, not a stated licence.

records.source: PostHog Handbook, Marketing
records.version_or_commit: unknown; living page, no revision id published
records.finding: A developer-tools company publishes its marketing operating rules in the open and reduces them to three: be opinionated, pull rather than push, and no sneaky shit. Marketing is organised as six small cross-functional teams (graphics, website, marketing, editorial, video, docs) rather than a channel hierarchy. The transferable move is that a small marketing function is a set of publishing teams with a stated stance, and the stance is what makes agent-generated content non-generic.
records.applicability_limits: Self-description by a venture-funded company selling to developers, with no reported outcome data attached to the principles, so it is a plausible exemplar rather than evidence that the approach works. Pull-not-push depends on having a technical audience that reads; it transfers badly to categories with no organic reading habit. The page is a live document with no version marker, so any citation dates immediately.
records.counter_evidence: The brand-building evidence tradition (EV-0368) argues that pull-only strategies underinvest in the mental availability that reaches non-searching buyers.
records.licence_evidence: "Overview - Handbook - PostHog" (URL resolves to posthog.com/handbook/marketing) states no licence. A full-text scan of the fully scrolled page for "licence/license/Creative Commons/copyright/rights reserved/MIT" returned zero matches. The page has a GitHub "edit this page" link but no licence terms on the page itself.

records.source: PostHog docs, Funnels
records.version_or_commit: unknown; living docs page, no revision id published
records.finding: A funnel is only defined once its parameters are declared: sequential versus strict-order versus any-order steps, exclusion steps that remove people from the whole funnel, and conversion measured either against the first step or against the previous step. Two teams quoting different conversion rates for the same product are usually quoting different parameter sets. So the pack should require the funnel definition to be stored as configuration next to the number, and any reported rate without it to be rejected.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor product documentation, and the page carries no warning against reading step drop-off as causal, which is the mistake most funnel reporting actually makes. Conversion-window semantics were not visible in the section retrieved, so that parameter remains unverified here.
records.licence_evidence: "Funnels - Docs - PostHog" states no licence. A full-text scan of the fully scrolled page found no licence or copyright statement (the only regex hits were the substring "mit" inside the words "limitative" and "limitation" in user comments). A GitHub source link is present but no licence terms.

records.source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for Marketing Science, Effective brand growth: acquisition or retention
records.study_design: Institute summary of longitudinal panel analyses of brand share change, resting on the double jeopardy empirical generalisation and citing Riebe, Wright, Stern and Sharp (2014) on service-category brands
records.population: Repeat-purchase consumer and service categories across many countries and decades
records.version_or_commit: undated institute page, timestamped roughly 2019 at access
records.licence: Copyright Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: Share growth comes overwhelmingly from acquiring category buyers rather than from reducing defection, and the institute puts acquisition at roughly twice the importance of retention. Under double jeopardy, small brands have both fewer buyers and slightly lower loyalty, and loyalty is largely a function of size rather than a lever that produces it. The decision rule is that a retention-first growth plan for a small brand is almost certainly the wrong plan, and reach to non-buyers is the default.
records.applicability_limits: The empirical base is repeat-purchase consumer goods and mass-market services, with large sample sizes but light-touch category coverage of B2B software, high-consideration purchases and subscription products where negative churn is a real mechanism. This is an institute summary rather than the underlying papers, all-rights-reserved so paraphrase only, and the institute has a commercial interest in the conclusion.
records.counter_evidence: Product-led and loop-based growth thinking (EV-0365) treats existing-user behaviour as the primary engine of new-user acquisition, which is not the same claim as retention-first but does put weight where Ehrenberg-Bass takes it away.

records.source: Binet and Field, The Long and the Short of It (IPA)
records.study_design: Analysis of the IPA Effectiveness Awards Databank, reported as 996 campaigns across roughly 700 brands and 83 sectors over three decades of submitted case studies
records.population: Mostly UK advertisers large enough to enter effectiveness awards
records.licence: unknown; IPA and WARC content is paywalled
records.finding: Brand-building and sales activation behave differently in time: activation produces a sharp short-lived lift, brand-building a slower compounding one, and the reported optimum split is around sixty per cent brand to forty per cent activation. The transferable principle is that a marketing plan must declare a time horizon per activity, because a single blended ROI number will always select activation and quietly starve the compounding half.
records.applicability_limits: An industry effectiveness report, recorded as blog because the enum has no value for it and the primary text could not be read. The primary text and the WARC commentary were both paywalled at this cutoff, so this record rests on secondary reporting and should be treated as a directional claim, not a verified one. The databank is self-selected award entries, which is a survivorship-biased sample; the 60:40 figure is an average across categories that the authors themselves have since qualified by category and business model, and it was derived in a pre-digital-dominant media landscape.
records.counter_evidence: The randomised-measurement literature (EV-0362) implies that the ROI figures underlying award case studies are themselves observational and likely biased, which weakens the arithmetic behind any specific split.
records.review: on-change-of:access to the IPA primary text

records.source: WCAG2Mobile: Applying WCAG 2.2 to Non-Web Mobile Apps (W3C)
records.version_or_commit: W3C Group Draft Note, published 6 May 2025, copyright line 2022-2025
records.licence: W3C Document Licence, paraphrase only, no verbatim reuse in pack text
records.finding: A native app needs a translated conformance model, not WCAG applied loosely: the unit of conformance becomes a screen or view rather than a page, web terms map onto platform terms, and the mobile-shaped criteria (orientation, pointer gestures, motion actuation, dragging movements, target size) carry most of the weight.
records.applicability_limits: A Group Draft Note, explicitly informative and not endorsed by W3C or its members, and it may be replaced at any time, so it can guide a mapping but cannot be cited as a conformance obligation. Covers Level A and AA only, and closed functionality is acknowledged as a gap.
records.counter_evidence: EN 301 549 clause 11 (EV-0371) is the instrument that actually binds in the EU and incorporates WCAG by reference at a version lagging this Note, so the two disagree on which WCAG version applies to an app today.

records.source: EN 301 549, Accessibility requirements for ICT products and services (ETSI/CEN/CENELEC)
records.version_or_commit: V3.2.1 (2021-03) is the version in force at inspection; a v4.1.x revision aligning clauses 9, 10 and 11 with WCAG 2.2 was reported in ETSI approval and was not yet published when checked
records.licence: ETSI copyright, freely downloadable, redistribution restricted; no open reuse licence
records.finding: Non-web software has its own clause (11) separate from web (9) and documents (10), and it adds obligations WCAG never states, chiefly interoperability with platform assistive technology and support for user preference settings, so a native app that only passes a WCAG mapping is still short of the standard.
records.applicability_limits: European instrument; it binds through the European Accessibility Act and public sector procurement, not everywhere. The in-force version references an older WCAG level than current, so a team that targets WCAG 2.2 is ahead of the standard rather than behind it. The revision date is a moving target and was not confirmed from a primary ETSI publication at inspection.
records.counter_evidence: WCAG2Mobile (EV-0370) maps to WCAG 2.2 and is more current in substance while carrying no legal force at all.

records.source: Apple App Review Guidelines
records.version_or_commit: unknown; the document declares itself a living document with no version handle or last-updated stamp on the page, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Proprietary, Apple copyright; freely readable, not reusable
records.finding: The binary is the unit of permission: rule 2.5.2 requires an app to be self-contained and forbids downloading code that introduces or changes features, so any remote-update mechanism is only lawful while it changes presentation rather than capability, and rule 4.2 rejects a wrapped website outright, which puts a floor under the web-shell strategy.
records.applicability_limits: Apple platforms only, and the rules that matter commercially (3.1.1 purchases, external link entitlements) now diverge by storefront, with the United States carved out, so a single global compliance answer no longer exists. No stated review timeline or appeal process on the page, so schedule risk cannot be planned from this source.
records.counter_evidence: Rule 4.7 permits whole classes of non-embedded software (mini apps, plug-ins, emulators) under conditions, which contradicts a naive reading of 2.5.2 as a total ban on remote code.

records.source: Apple App Store Transparency Report, 2025
records.study_design: Vendor census of its own moderation decisions across the reporting year, self-reported counts with no external audit and no published methodology for category assignment
records.population: 9,100,620 submissions reviewed across 175 countries and regions during 2025
records.version_or_commit: 2025 reporting year edition, copyright 2026 Apple Inc, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Proprietary, Apple copyright; no reuse licence stated
records.finding: Rejection is the normal case, not the exception: 2,093,244 of 9,100,620 submissions were rejected, roughly one in four, and the largest single reason by a wide margin is Performance at 1,354,418, ahead of Legal 495,673, Design 415,532, Business 283,820 and Safety 151,159, so a release plan should budget at least one rejection cycle and should treat crash-free and complete-on-arrival builds as the highest-yield mitigation.
records.applicability_limits: Self-reported and self-categorised; Performance is a coarse bucket that mixes crashes, bugs, broken links and placeholder content, so it cannot be decomposed into engineering actions from this source. Counts are submissions, not distinct apps, so a repeatedly resubmitted app inflates the number. Appeal figures are for removals, not rejections: 26,305 removal appeals produced 423 restorations, which says nothing about rejection appeals.
records.counter_evidence: The Review Guidelines (EV-0372) promise consistent approvals and rejections, which the 1.6 per cent removal appeal success rate does not obviously support in either direction.

records.source: Apple App Store Connect help, Release a version update in phases
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live help page, no version or revision stamp, inspected 2026-08-03)
records.licence: Proprietary, Apple copyright; freely readable, not reusable
records.finding: Apple's phased release is a fixed seven-day ramp of 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 then 100 per cent that applies only to users with automatic updates, while anyone can fetch the new version manually at any time, so the ramp bounds blast radius weakly and cannot be used as a control plane; pausing is allowed for up to thirty days in total across any number of pauses, and there is no rollback, only a new version.
records.applicability_limits: Apple platforms only. The percentages are not developer-selectable, the cohort is not steerable, and there is no automatic halt on a metric, so this is not progressive delivery in the Argo Rollouts sense (EV-0204). Removing the app from sale terminates phasing permanently for that version.
records.counter_evidence: Google Play's staged rollout (EV-0375) lets the developer choose the percentage and halt on demand, so the two stores do not offer the same release control and a single cross-platform release runbook cannot assume symmetry.
records.review: on-change-of:app store connect phased release mechanics

records.source: Google Play Console Help, Release app updates with staged rollouts
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live help page, no revision date displayed, inspected 2026-08-03)
records.licence: Proprietary, Google copyright; freely readable, not reusable
