records.finding: Play gives the developer the percentage dial and a halt button, but the halt only stops further delivery: users who already took the update keep it, there is no rollback, and the documented remedy is to ship a fixed bundle, so the only real containment lever is how small the first slice is and how fast a fix can be built and reviewed.
records.applicability_limits: Applies to updates, not first launches, so a new app gets no gradual exposure at all. Country scope cannot be narrowed once started. No metric-driven automatic halt is described, so the trigger has to come from the team's own telemetry.
records.counter_evidence: Apple's phased release (EV-0374) fixes the schedule and removes the dial, the mirror-image trade of control against simplicity.

records.source: Android Developers, Meet Google Play's target API level requirement
records.version_or_commit: State at inspection 2026-08-03: from 31 August 2026 new apps and updates must target API 36 (Android 16); existing apps must target API 35 to stay visible to new users on newer devices; extension to 1 November 2026 available on request
records.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the documentation text per the site footer convention; code samples Apache-2.0. Verify per page before reuse.
records.finding: Distribution decays without maintenance: an app that stops shipping does not merely stagnate, it becomes invisible to new users on current devices as the target API floor rises annually, so a maintained release train is a distribution requirement and the annual SDK bump belongs on the roadmap as fixed work, not as discretionary upkeep.
records.applicability_limits: Google Play only; sideloaded and enterprise-private distribution is exempt, and the consequence is reduced visibility rather than removal, so an app with a stable installed base degrades slowly rather than failing outright. Deadlines shift each year and differ for Wear, TV, Automotive and XR.

records.source: Expo documentation, EAS Update introduction
records.version_or_commit: page modification date shown as 22 July 2026, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: unknown; no licence stated on the page
records.finding: Over-the-air updating draws a hard line at the native boundary: JavaScript, styling, assets, copy and translations can ship without a store round trip, while native code, native dependencies, permissions and SDK upgrades cannot, and the vendor itself restates that store rules still apply to behaviour changes, so OTA buys latency on presentation and never buys exemption from review.
records.applicability_limits: Specific to the Expo and React Native runtime model; the runtime version pinning that makes it safe also means an OTA channel is only valid for binaries built from a compatible native runtime, which fragments the fleet. Does not describe how a bad update is rolled back or what fraction of users take an update before relaunch.
records.counter_evidence: Apple rule 2.5.2 (EV-0372) forbids downloaded code that introduces or changes features, so the safe envelope for OTA is narrower than the technical capability, and the vendor doc does not draw that line for you.

records.source: Kleppmann, Wiggins, van Hardenberg and McGranaghan, Local-first software: you own your data, in spite of the cloud (Onward! 2019)
records.study_design: Position paper plus qualitative evaluation: seven stated ideals used as a scoring rubric against existing technology classes (files, web apps, Dropbox, Git, Firebase, CouchDB) together with the authors' own prototype experience; no controlled measurement
records.version_or_commit: April 2019 essay, Onward! 2019 proceedings version, inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: unknown; no explicit licence notice on the essay page, ACM proceedings version under ACM terms
records.finding: Offline capability is one ideal among seven, and the other six (multi-device, seamless collaboration, longevity, security and privacy, user control, no spinners) drive most of the architecture, so a decision to go offline-first should be argued against a named subset of these ideals rather than as a single yes or no about the network.
records.applicability_limits: A 2019 position paper by CRDT authors evaluating CRDTs, so it is advocacy with a stake; no measurement, no user study, and the technology landscape it scores has moved. Its own caution that CRDTs were not yet advisable in place of a proven backend is now seven years old and cannot be relied on either way.
records.counter_evidence: PowerSync (EV-0383) and Electric (EV-0382) both ship server-authoritative designs that abandon several ideals deliberately and are in production, which suggests the ideals are a menu rather than a package.

records.source: Kleppmann and Beresford, A Conflict-Free Replicated JSON Datatype
records.study_design: Algorithm design with formal operational semantics and convergence proof; no empirical evaluation of user-perceived merge quality
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:1608.03960, submitted 13 August 2016, final revision 15 August 2017; a peer-reviewed version appeared in IEEE TPDS, not verified at inspection
records.licence: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence; paraphrase, do not reproduce figures or text
records.finding: The guarantee a JSON CRDT actually provides is convergence without lost updates under arbitrary network ordering, proved for nested maps and lists with insert, delete and assign; it does not provide a guarantee that the converged value is the one a user or an invariant wanted, which is a separate problem the algorithm does not address.
records.applicability_limits: Formal result about a data type, not about an application: uniqueness constraints, monetary balances, referential integrity and approval states are all outside what convergence buys. Implementations differ from the paper in storage and garbage collection, so performance claims here transfer to no shipping library directly.
records.counter_evidence: PowerSync (EV-0383) states plainly that there is no single correct choice for handling write failures, which is precisely the space convergence proofs leave empty.

records.source: Automerge
records.version_or_commit: Automerge 3 line per README; 1,600 commits on main at inspection; exact release tag and last commit date not confirmed
records.finding: A mature CRDT library sells three separable things, the merge semantics, a compressed on-disk format and a sync protocol, and the memory and storage work (roughly a tenfold memory reduction claimed for the version 3 line) is where the practical viability lives, so a library evaluation should test the format and sync protocol on realistic document sizes rather than accepting the merge story alone.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor's own performance claim, not independently measured here. The maintainers state the Rust API is low level and thinly documented and is shaped around the JavaScript wrapper, which matters a great deal if the target is a shared core for iOS and Android rather than a browser app. Staffing is small, two full-time maintainers plus contributors.
records.counter_evidence: The original local-first essay by the same group (EV-0378) flagged unbounded change history as a structural performance problem, and mitigation rather than elimination is what the library offers.

records.source: Yjs
records.version_or_commit: 2,264 commits on main at inspection; exact release tag and last commit date not confirmed
records.finding: The maintainers state the structural cost openly, that text-suitable CRDTs only grow, and the engineering answer is struct merging, content deletion and tombstone garbage collection under stated conditions, so a client that stores a CRDT document must plan compaction and a storage budget as first-class concerns rather than as later tuning.
records.applicability_limits: Optimised for shared text editing under the YATA algorithm; the shape of the win does not transfer automatically to record-oriented business data. Garbage collection is conditional, and the conditions were not enumerated at inspection, so the growth bound cannot be stated from this source.
records.counter_evidence: Automerge (EV-0380) makes competing performance claims and the two projects publish benchmarks against each other, so neither figure is neutral.

records.source: ElectricSQL, electric
records.version_or_commit: status stated as 1.0 with a March 2025 reference; 2,231 commits on main at inspection
records.finding: A serious sync project narrowed its own scope to a read-path engine with partial replication through shapes, leaving writes to the application, which is evidence that the hard and unshippable part of offline-first is the write path, not the read path, and that a team can take most of the offline benefit by syncing reads and keeping writes conventional.
records.applicability_limits: Postgres-sourced only. The repository page does not state the history behind the scope change or any write-path guidance, so the inference about why is mine and rests on the shape of the product rather than on a maintainer statement. Version 1.0 status was read from the page, not from a release tag.
records.counter_evidence: Automerge and Yjs (EV-0380, EV-0381) take the opposite bet, that bidirectional convergence is the product, and both are actively maintained with real users.

records.source: PowerSync documentation, Consistency
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live doc, no version or revision stamp, inspected 2026-08-03)
records.licence: unknown; no licence stated on the page
records.finding: A server-authoritative design buys away local conflict resolution by construction: a blocking FIFO upload queue holds the client at its last confirmed checkpoint until the backend acknowledges every pending mutation, giving causal-plus consistency, and the vendor states outright that there is no single correct choice for handling write failures, so the conflict policy is application code the team must write and test.
records.applicability_limits: The same mechanism that removes local conflicts creates a head-of-line blocking failure mode: an unacknowledged mutation stalls the client's whole sync state, so a poorly behaved backend degrades the app globally rather than locally. Causal-plus is claimed with reference to independent testing that was not examined here.
records.counter_evidence: CRDT libraries (EV-0380, EV-0381) merge without a round trip and therefore have no head-of-line blocking, at the cost of accepting a converged value nobody chose.

records.source: React Native, repository and New Architecture documentation
records.version_or_commit: 41,284 commits on main at inspection; 0.86.2 shown as latest stable with 0.87.0 release candidates in flight; release dates on the releases page were not parsed reliably and are not asserted
records.finding: The platform completed a rewrite of its own interop layer, with the New Architecture default from 0.76 after opt-in from 0.68, while keeping an opt-out flag and declining to declare the legacy path deprecated, which is the honest cost model for a bridged framework: the seam between shared code and platform code is itself a long-lived migration surface that the team inherits.
records.applicability_limits: Version numbers move monthly on a zero-major scheme, so semantic versioning expectations (EV-0171) do not apply and every upgrade is potentially breaking. The New Architecture default status was read from vendor documentation, not measured, and third-party native module readiness is the real gate and is not visible from this source.
records.counter_evidence: Flutter (EV-0385) avoids the platform-widget seam entirely by rendering its own widgets, which removes this class of migration at the cost of never inheriting platform behaviour for free.

records.source: Flutter
records.version_or_commit: 90,700 commits on master at inspection; 3.44 referenced as current on the release documentation with a May 2026 target; exact stable tag and date not confirmed because the archive table loads dynamically
records.licence: BSD-3-Clause; note the tool may download resources from Google servers and use is tied to Google terms of service
records.finding: Owning the renderer is the defining trade: compiling to ARM machine code for iOS and Android and to JavaScript or WebAssembly for the web with its own 2D graphics stack gives one behaviour everywhere, which is exactly why platform conventions, accessibility services and system controls arrive only as far as the framework has reimplemented them.
records.applicability_limits: Breadth of claimed targets (mobile, web, desktop) is not uniform in maturity and the repository does not grade them; Impeller is named without a maturity statement. Governance is single-vendor with a corporate dependency baked into the tooling terms.
records.counter_evidence: Kotlin Multiplatform (EV-0386) publishes a per-target stability grade instead, which is the more auditable disclosure even where the underlying maturity is similar.

records.source: Kotlin Multiplatform documentation, Supported platforms
records.version_or_commit: page dated 10 September 2025, inspected 2026-08-03; core Kotlin Multiplatform Stable for Android, iOS, JVM desktop, server and Kotlin/JS, Beta for Kotlin/Wasm, watchOS and tvOS; Compose Multiplatform Stable for Android, iOS and desktop, Beta for Wasm
records.licence: Apache-2.0 for the Kotlin project; documentation reuse terms not stated on the page
records.finding: Publishing a stability grade per target rather than a single project maturity is what makes a cross-platform bet auditable, and it separates the two decisions cleanly: sharing logic across Android and iOS is a Stable choice, sharing the user interface is a second and independent choice that carries its own grade and can be declined per surface.
records.applicability_limits: Self-graded by the vendor with no published criteria for what earns Stable, and the page carries no version alignment to a Kotlin or Compose release, so a grade cannot be pinned to a dependency version. Watch and TV targets remain Beta, which matters for any product with a companion surface.
records.counter_evidence: Neither Flutter nor React Native publishes a comparable per-target grade, so the absence of a grade elsewhere is not evidence of lower maturity, only of less disclosure.

records.source: Android Developers, Accessibility principles
records.version_or_commit: unknown (live doc, Compose-oriented revision, no revision stamp, inspected 2026-08-03)
records.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for documentation text and Apache-2.0 for samples per the site convention; verify per page before reuse
records.finding: Platform accessibility is expressed as a semantics tree the developer edits deliberately, with content descriptions, descendant merging, explicit heading and pane-title semantics, custom actions with human labels, and null descriptions for decoration, so the reviewable artefact on a native client is the semantics declaration in code, not a rendered screenshot.
records.applicability_limits: The page gives no numeric thresholds at all, no touch target minimum and no contrast ratio, and defers testing to a separate page, so it cannot supply the measurable floor a check needs; those numbers have to come from WCAG 2.2 (EV-0027) via the mobile mapping (EV-0370). Guidance is Compose-shaped and thinner for View-based code.
records.counter_evidence: EN 301 549 clause 11 (EV-0371) requires assistive technology interoperability and user preference support that this page treats as implicit platform behaviour rather than as a developer obligation.

records.source: Apple WWDC 2023 session 10035, Perform accessibility audits for your app (XCTest performAccessibilityAudit)
records.version_or_commit: WWDC 2023 session, capability shipped in Xcode 15; the session page and the current API reference were not retrievable by plain fetch at inspection and the capability description rests on secondary write-ups
records.licence: Proprietary, Apple copyright; freely viewable, not reusable
records.finding: An automated accessibility audit exists inside the platform test runner and can be scoped to an app, a screen or a single element with selectable audit types, covering missing labels, clipped text, contrast and Dynamic Type support, which makes a native accessibility gate a normal failing test rather than a manual review ritual.
records.applicability_limits: Primary sources could not be fetched, so this record should be re-verified against the current XCTest reference before any pack text quotes it. No coverage figure is published, so the proportion of real defects it catches is unknown on this platform, unlike the web where a figure exists and is contested (EV-0236 at about 57 per cent against roughly a third in EV-0104). Apple platforms only; the Android equivalents are separate tools.
records.counter_evidence: WebAIM Million (EV-0235) states that no detected errors does not mean accessible, and that caution applies at least as strongly here where no coverage figure exists at all.

records.source: APCA in a Nutshell (Myndex Research, Advanced Perceptual Contrast Algorithm)
records.version_or_commit: unknown (documentation page carries no version or revision date at access)
records.licence: unknown (no reuse licence stated on the documentation page; the algorithm itself is distributed under separate Myndex terms)
records.finding: Perceived text contrast depends on polarity, font weight and spatial frequency, not on a single luminance ratio. APCA returns a signed lightness contrast (Lc) that pairs with a minimum font size and weight, and it deliberately scores dark-background and light-background pairs differently for the same nominal ratio. The practical consequence for a dark-register house style is that a WCAG 2 ratio quoted for light text on a dark ground is not a reliable statement about how readable that text actually is.
records.applicability_limits: Applies to text on solid backgrounds on self-luminous displays under typical office ambient light. Not a conformance standard, so it cannot be used to claim accessibility compliance. Says nothing about non-text contrast, gradients, translucent overlays or text sitting on animated light fields, which is exactly where a light-system house style puts pressure.
records.counter_evidence: APCA was removed from the WCAG 3 working draft in 2023 and has not been reinstated as the chosen method, so its thresholds have no normative standing; see EV-0390.

records.source: Adrian Roselli, WCAG3 Contrast as of April 2026
records.licence: unknown (personal site, no reuse licence stated)
records.finding: The visual contrast requirement was moved out of the WCAG 3 working draft in July 2023 and the replacement method is still undetermined. The workable position for a house style is two layers: WCAG 2.2 AA as the compliance floor that can be automated and asserted, and a perceptual method used only as an internal readability check that never appears in a conformance claim.
records.applicability_limits: A practitioner reading of an unfinished standards process, correct only at its date. Does not itself measure anything. WCAG 3 is not expected to be a Recommendation for years, so any decision keyed to its arrival is a decision deferred indefinitely.
records.counter_evidence: Vendor and community guidance from the same period presents APCA as though it were the WCAG 3 method; that framing is not supported by the Working Group record.

records.source: Bateman, Mandryk, Gutwin, Genest, McDine and Brooks, Useful Junk? The Effects of Visual Embellishment on Comprehension and Memorability of Charts (CHI 2010)
records.study_design: Within-subjects lab experiment comparing heavily embellished charts against plain equivalents on interpretation accuracy and on recall immediately and after roughly two to three weeks.
records.population: Adult university-recruited participants; exact sample size not verified from the hosted copy at access.
records.licence: unknown (ACM copyright; this is a third-party hosted copy, no reuse licence stated)
records.finding: Embellishment did not cost interpretation accuracy, and it improved long-term recall of both the chart topic and its message. Minimalism is therefore a defensible default for accuracy and a weak default for memorability. The decision rule that survives is to separate the two jobs: charts that must be read precisely stay austere, and the one figure a piece is meant to be remembered by is allowed a distinguishing device.
records.applicability_limits: Single study, small sample, one illustrator's hand-drawn style as the embellished condition, static print-like charts, no interaction and no accessibility measurement. It does not license arbitrary decoration, and it says nothing about dashboards, repeated figures or charts read under time pressure.
records.counter_evidence: The minimalist tradition it argues against is widely held and later replications report mixed results; the house rule that no ornament may overlap a line or displace a datum is untouched by this finding.

records.source: Dyson and Haselgrove, The influence of reading speed and line length on the effectiveness of reading from screen (International Journal of Human-Computer Studies, 2001)
records.study_design: Controlled experiment crossing line length (roughly 25, 55 and 100 characters per line) with instructed reading speed (normal and fast), measuring comprehension, reading rate and scrolling behaviour.
records.population: Adult readers reading continuous text from screen in a laboratory setting.
records.licence: unknown (Elsevier copyright; abstract page only, paraphrase only)
records.finding: A medium measure of roughly 55 characters per line produced the best comprehension, beating both a narrow measure and a long one, and the advantage was not explained away by reading rate. Comprehension and raw speed do not optimise at the same measure, so a house style must say which it is optimising for. For long-form argument the answer is comprehension, which puts the reading column near the low end of the usual 45 to 75 character advice rather than the high end.
records.applicability_limits: Cathode-ray displays, 2001 typography, scrolling rather than paged reading, comprehension measured by multiple choice recall. Says nothing about mobile viewports, variable fonts, dense reference material or the effect of marginalia hanging outside the measure.
records.counter_evidence: Later work, including Shaikh and Chaparro on online news, reports faster reading at longer measures and reader preferences that do not match measured performance, so preference and comprehension can point in opposite directions.

records.source: Piepenbrock, Mayr, Buchner, Positive display polarity is advantageous for both younger and older adults (Ergonomics, 2013)
records.study_design: Controlled experiment measuring visual acuity and proofreading performance under positive polarity (dark text on light ground) and negative polarity (light text on dark ground), across two age groups, with pupil size recorded.
records.population: Younger and older adults with normal or corrected vision.
records.licence: unknown (Taylor and Francis copyright; abstract record only, paraphrase only)
records.finding: Positive polarity gave better acuity and better proofreading performance for both age groups, with smaller pupil size predicting the advantage. The effect concentrates at small character sizes near the limit of acuity. The design rule this yields is not that dark registers are wrong, but that a dark register buys back its cost only by spending on size, weight and measured contrast in the smallest text, which is exactly the annotation voice a technical house style leans on.
records.applicability_limits: Proofreading and acuity tasks under controlled office lighting on displays of the period, not sustained reading for pleasure, not low-light or outdoor use, and not readers with cataracts or light sensitivity where the advantage can reverse. Effect sizes are largest for very small type and shrink as type grows.
records.counter_evidence: The advantage is much weaker or absent at larger sizes, and some visually impaired users perform better in dark mode, so a blanket ban on dark registers is not supported.

records.source: Nielsen Norman Group, Dark Mode versus Light Mode: Which Is Better? (Raluca Budiu)
records.study_design: Narrative review of the display-polarity literature, not new data collection.
records.licence: Copyright 1998 to 2026 Nielsen Norman Group, all rights reserved; paraphrase only, no verbatim reuse
records.finding: For users with normal or corrected vision, light mode supports better performance most of the time, while some users with specific impairments do better in dark mode. The operational conclusion is that register is a preference to be offered rather than a truth to be asserted, and that a dark-first house style should treat a light register as a supported variant rather than an afterthought.
records.applicability_limits: A secondary synthesis, not a primary study, and its evidence base is the same small polarity literature. Written before the current generation of high-brightness displays and before dark mode became the platform default on mobile, so ambient-light assumptions may have drifted.
records.counter_evidence: Platform design languages, including Apple and Google, ship dark registers as first-class and report user preference for them; preference and measured performance disagree here.

records.source: web.dev, How to create high-performance CSS animations
records.licence: Content CC BY 4.0; code samples Apache-2.0
records.finding: Animation should be restricted to transform and opacity so the work stays on the compositing stage. Animating geometry or paint properties, including background-position, width, top and continuous filters, forces layout or paint on every frame. This is the mechanical justification for a written property whitelist: the whitelist is not taste, it is the set of properties that can be animated without a per-frame repaint.
records.applicability_limits: Browser-engine guidance of its date. Compositing rules differ between engines and change over time, and an element can still be forced to repaint if it is not isolated or intersects effects that demand repainting. Gives no budget for how many animated layers a page may carry.
records.counter_evidence: Modern engines can composite some filter and clip-path changes, so the whitelist is conservative rather than exact; measurement on target hardware beats the rule where the two disagree.

records.source: web.dev, Stick to Compositor-Only Properties and Manage Layer Count
records.version_or_commit: unknown (no update date exposed on the page at access)
records.licence: Content CC BY 4.0; code samples Apache-2.0
records.finding: Promoting elements to their own compositor layer is what makes transform and opacity animation cheap, but each layer costs memory and management, so promotion must be budgeted rather than sprinkled. A house style that puts ambient light fields, conduits and hover blooms on many elements at once is spending layers, and the budget belongs in the written rules next to the alpha budgets.
records.applicability_limits: Layer promotion heuristics are engine-specific and undocumented in detail; the article gives no numeric ceiling, so any house number is a local calibration rather than a derived limit. Low-memory mobile devices are the binding constraint and are not measured here.

records.source: Val Head, Designing Safer Web Animation For Motion Sensitivity (A List Apart, issue 428)
records.licence: unknown (A List Apart retains article copyright; paraphrase only)
records.finding: Motion that triggers vestibular symptoms is characterised by properties, not by taste: large surface area in motion, parallax and depth cues, spinning, and unexpected scroll-coupled movement. Small, local, opacity-led motion is comparatively safe. This gives a discrimination rule a checker can approximate: judge motion by how much of the viewport moves and whether it is tied to scroll, not by how tasteful it looks.
records.applicability_limits: Practitioner synthesis of clinical background rather than primary experiment, and it predates the prefers-reduced-motion media query becoming widely supported. It cannot tell you a safe threshold in pixels or degrees, so any numeric budget remains a judgement.
records.counter_evidence: Honouring prefers-reduced-motion is often treated as sufficient, but the setting is unset for most users, so a page that is only safe under the query is not safe by default.

records.source: W3C, CSS Properties and Values API Level 1
records.licence: W3C Software and Document License (permissive document licence); paraphrase only, no verbatim copying of spec text
records.finding: Registering a custom property with a declared syntax, initial value and inheritance behaviour is what makes it animatable and interpolable. Any house effect built on an animated angle, length or colour custom property, such as a conic border beam or a travelling gradient, depends on this registration; without it the value is an untyped token and the animation silently does nothing. The rule is that a house kit declares its animated custom properties in one place, as part of the token layer.
records.applicability_limits: Still a Working Draft, so behaviour may change and the JavaScript registration path differs from the at-rule path in older engines. Registration does not make an animation cheap; a registered colour or angle can still drive a per-frame repaint.
records.review: on-change-of:CSS Properties and Values API Level 1 status

records.source: W3C, CSS Text Module Level 4
records.licence: W3C Software and Document License (permissive document licence); paraphrase only
records.finding: Line-breaking quality is now a declared property rather than a manual craft: balance equalises line lengths across a short block, and pretty optimises break quality at greater layout cost. Both are explicitly permitted to be limited or ignored by an implementation, which means a house rule can require them as a hint but must never depend on them for layout correctness. Balance belongs on short display lines; applying it to body paragraphs is both against the property's intent and a performance cost.
records.applicability_limits: Working Draft, so values and their exact behaviour can change. Implementations differ in the number of lines they will balance and may decline entirely, so visual results are not reproducible across engines and cannot be screenshot-tested strictly.

records.source: W3C, CSS Color Module Level 4
records.licence: W3C Software and Document License (permissive document licence); paraphrase only
records.finding: Perceptually uniform spaces, Oklab and OkLCh in particular, plus defined interpolation and gamut-mapping rules, make a surface ladder derivable rather than eyeballed: hold chroma and hue, step lightness evenly, and the steps are equally distinguishable. Doing the same in sRGB hexadecimal produces ladders with invisible steps at one end and jumps at the other, which is the usual cause of a grey-on-grey ladder nobody can see.
records.applicability_limits: Candidate Recommendation Draft rather than Recommendation. Wide-gamut colours require gamut mapping on sRGB displays, so a ladder that is even in OkLCh can compress once mapped. Perceptual uniformity is a model of average vision and does not guarantee legibility, which still has to be measured as contrast.
records.counter_evidence: Evenly spaced lightness steps are not evenly perceived on every display or in every ambient light, so cheap-display verification remains a separate check.
records.review: on-change-of:CSS Color Module Level 4 reaching Recommendation

records.source: W3C, CSS Masking Module Level 1
records.licence: W3C Software and Document License (permissive document licence); paraphrase only
records.finding: mask-composite with the exclude operator is the standard way to cut a filled shape down to a one-pixel ring, which is what turns a gradient into a border beam without a third pseudo-element. Because masking is a paint-time operation on the whole box, an animated mask is not compositor-cheap; the animation should drive a registered angle or a transform underneath a static mask rather than animating the mask itself.
records.applicability_limits: Candidate Recommendation Draft since 2021 with uneven engine support and prefixed legacy syntax in some browsers, so a masked ring needs a documented fallback. Masks are not accessibility-neutral: a masked decorative element must be hidden from assistive technology explicitly.

records.source: Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek and Brown, Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression (Behaviour and Information Technology, 2006)
records.study_design: Three linked experiments rating the visual appeal of web homepages shown for 500 milliseconds and, in the third, 50 milliseconds, testing reliability of the judgement and its relation to specific design dimensions.
records.population: Adult participants recruited at a Canadian university.
records.version_or_commit: Behaviour and Information Technology volume 25, issue 2, 2006, pages 115 to 126
records.licence: unknown (Taylor and Francis copyright; abstract page only, paraphrase only)
records.finding: Visual appeal judgements form within about 50 milliseconds and are stable on re-exposure, which means the impression is made before any copy is read. This supports spending the design budget on what is visible in the first screen, the type ladder and the opening furniture, rather than on effects that only appear after scrolling. It does not support the stronger claim that appeal predicts usefulness.
records.applicability_limits: Homepages of the mid 2000s, appeal ratings only, no task performance, no measure of trust or conversion, and a student population. The finding is about how fast a judgement forms, not about which judgement is correct or whether it persists after use.
records.counter_evidence: First impressions are revised by use, and a page that wins at 50 milliseconds can still fail on comprehension; the aesthetic-usability effect is a bias to be watched, not a design goal.

records.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works
records.population: UK central government digital services assessed against the Service Standard
records.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0, Crown copyright
records.finding: Discovery is time-boxed and output-typed, not open-ended. The stated rules are: do not start building the service during discovery, expect roughly four to eight weeks, and exit only when you can state the problem in a form that is not a restatement of somebody's proposed solution, name hard and soft constraints, map what already exists across the problem space, and say how success will be measured. The load-bearing rule is that deciding to stop at the end of discovery counts as a successful discovery, which makes an explicit kill option part of the phase definition rather than a failure mode.
records.applicability_limits: Written for large public-sector services with statutory duties, a fixed assessment gate and a funded multidisciplinary team. The four-to-eight-week box is calibrated to that funding shape and is far too long for a small venture deciding on a single feature. The phase language also assumes a hand-off to a separate alpha team, which does not exist in a solo or agent-driven venture. The page has not been substantively updated since 2021 and predates agentic development entirely.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0405 and EV-0420 both suggest that for anything with live traffic, a cheap experiment resolves value questions faster and more reliably than a research phase of any length.
records.review: on-change-of:the GOV.UK Service Manual agile delivery section or the Service Standard

records.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, User research in discovery
records.population: UK central government service teams
records.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0, Crown copyright
records.finding: Discovery research is end-to-end and coverage-driven rather than sample-size-driven: the instruction is to consider every way users interact with the service including offline and assisted routes, and to include disabled users and users with low digital skills from the first round rather than as a later accessibility pass. The principle that transfers is that the recruitment frame, not the participant count, is what determines whether a discovery can be wrong.
records.applicability_limits: Public services have a legal duty to serve everyone and a captive population that cannot go elsewhere. A commercial venture choosing a niche can legitimately exclude segments, so the universal-coverage rule becomes a deliberate scoping decision rather than an obligation. The guidance also assumes access to real users, which a pre-launch venture does not have.
records.review: on-change-of:the GOV.UK Service Manual user research section

records.source: Kohavi, Deng, Frasca, Walker, Xu and Pohlmann, Online Controlled Experiments at Large Scale (KDD 2013)
records.study_design: Industrial experience report over a large corpus of randomised online controlled experiments run on a shared platform
records.population: Microsoft properties, principally Bing, plus platform-wide experiment history
records.licence: ACM copyright, paywalled; paraphrase only, no reproduction of text or figures
records.finding: The base rate for ideas is the central result: roughly one third of experimented ideas move the target metric positively and significantly, roughly one third are flat, and roughly one third are negative, with Bing reporting a lower hit rate still. Expert judgement inside the team does not predict which third an idea lands in. The decision rule that follows is that any prioritisation scheme which assumes the team can rank ideas by expected value is calibrating against a signal that measurably is not there, so throughput of cheap tests dominates accuracy of ranking.
records.applicability_limits: The population is very high-traffic consumer search and portal surfaces where a statistically powered experiment finishes in days and effect sizes of fractions of a per cent matter commercially. A venture with tens or hundreds of users cannot power a test on any metric that matters, so the one-third base rate is a prior about idea quality rather than a runnable method. The paper predates LLM-assisted ideation, so it says nothing about whether agent-generated ideas have the same base rate.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0406 by the same lead author documents that naive experimentation produces confidently wrong answers, so the throughput argument only holds when the platform enforces trustworthy analysis.

records.source: Kohavi, Deng and Vermeer, A/B Testing Intuition Busters: Common Misunderstandings in Online Controlled Experiments (KDD 2022)
records.study_design: Methodological paper: enumerates intuitive but statistically wrong practices and derives the correct reasoning, drawn from platform experience across several companies
records.population: Industrial experimentation platforms and their users, including tool vendors and agencies
records.version_or_commit: KDD 2022 proceedings version, DOI 10.1145/3534678.3539160, landing page retrieved 2026-08-03
records.licence: ACM copyright for the paper; landing page unlicensed. Paraphrase only
records.finding: Several practices that vendors present as sensible are shown to be wrong by construction, including stopping a test when it first crosses significance and treating small-sample results as directional. The transferable rule is that an experiment is only evidence if the stopping rule, the metric and the segmentation were fixed before the data arrived, and that a surprisingly large effect should first be treated as an instrumentation bug rather than a discovery.
records.applicability_limits: Aimed at teams that already run experiments at volume with a platform enforcing guardrails. A venture running one manual test a quarter gets the discipline but none of the automated protection, so the failure modes described are more likely, not less. Scope is quantitative online experiments only and gives no guidance on qualitative discovery.

records.source: Faulkner, Beyond the five-user assumption: Benefits of increased sample sizes in usability testing
records.study_design: Empirical resampling study: 60 participants tested on one interface, then random subsets of 5, 10, 20 and more drawn repeatedly to measure the distribution of problem-detection rates
records.population: 60 usability test participants on a single web application, 2003
records.version_or_commit: Behavior Research Methods, Instruments and Computers 35(3), 379 to 383, 2003; DOI 10.3758/BF03195514
records.finding: Small usability samples are not merely less thorough, they are wildly variable. Across random sets of five participants the share of known problems found ranged from 99 per cent down to 55 per cent. Ten participants raised the worst-case floor to about 80 per cent and twenty raised it to about 95 per cent. The decision rule is to reason about the worst case of a sample rather than its average, because a team only ever runs one sample and has no way to tell which one it drew.
records.applicability_limits: One interface, one problem set, one 2003 web application, and the denominator is problems found by the full 60, so problems nobody found are invisible to the analysis. It measures problem detection in a moderated lab task and says nothing about whether a demand exists or whether users would pay. Generalising the exact percentages to a different interface class is not supported.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0408 argues from a diminishing-returns model that five is the efficient stopping point when the alternative is more iterations, which is a different objective function rather than a contradicted result.

records.source: Nielsen Norman Group, Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users
records.study_design: Argument from a fitted mathematical model of cumulative problem discovery, N times one minus L to the power n, with L taken as about 0.31
records.population: Aggregated usability studies available to the authors in the 1990s
records.version_or_commit: published 2000-03-18, no revision date shown, retrieved 2026-08-03
records.licence: Copyright Nielsen Norman Group, all rights reserved. Paraphrase only
records.finding: Given a fixed budget, three rounds of five users beat one round of fifteen, because each round changes the design and therefore changes the problem set being sampled. The stated caveats matter more than the headline: a single participant can mislead, and distinct user groups need three to four participants each. The transferable principle is that iteration count, not participant count, is the variable to spend on when the design is still moving.
records.applicability_limits: The model assumes an independent, equal detection probability per problem per user, which is why EV-0407 finds the variance the model hides. It applies to finding usability defects in an existing design, not to establishing whether the problem is worth solving. It is twenty-six years old, has never been revised, and is routinely cited to justify five interviews in situations the article does not cover.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0407 directly measures the variance this model averages away and finds the worst case of a five-user sample is poor.
records.review: on-change-of:any NN/g revision or retraction of the five-user article

records.source: Mavin, Wilkinson, Harwood and Novak, Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax (EARS), and the official EARS guide
records.study_design: Practice-derived notation, developed while analysing airworthiness regulations for a jet engine control system; first published at IEEE RE'09
records.population: Safety-critical aerospace requirements at Rolls-Royce, subsequently adopted more widely
records.version_or_commit: RE'09 paper, 2009; official guide site retrieved 2026-08-03
records.licence: IEEE copyright for the paper; guide site licence not stated, treat as unknown. Paraphrase only
records.finding: Constraining requirement prose to a fixed clause order removes most ambiguity without leaving natural language. The template is: while optional preconditions, when an optional trigger, the named system shall produce one or more responses, with exactly zero or one trigger and exactly one named system per requirement. The forcing function is that a requirement which cannot be written in the template is usually not a requirement but a wish, a design decision or two requirements stuck together.
records.applicability_limits: Derived from and validated on safety-critical embedded control, where the system boundary and the trigger set are both closed and knowable. Product discovery deals in requirements whose triggers are user intentions, and forcing those into shall-statements too early converts an open question into a false certainty. EARS constrains form and does nothing to establish whether the requirement should exist.
records.review: on-change-of:a revised EARS specification or a successor notation adopted by the official guide

records.source: Rodden, Hutchinson and Fu, Measuring the User Experience on a Large Scale: User-Centered Metrics for Web Applications (CHI 2010)
records.study_design: Framework paper with applied case studies from internal product teams
records.population: Google web application teams, circa 2010
records.licence: ACM copyright; Google Research landing page unlicensed. Paraphrase only
records.finding: The durable contribution is the goals-signals-metrics ladder rather than the five HEART categories. You state the goal for the feature, name the observable signal that would move if the goal were met, then derive the metric. Categories exist to stop teams defaulting to whatever the analytics package happens to count. The rule for discovery is that a proposal without a stated signal is untestable, and a metric chosen before its goal is a vanity metric by construction.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes enough traffic that ratio metrics are stable and enough instrumentation that arbitrary signals can be collected. At very low volume the ladder still disciplines the argument but the metrics will be noise. The categories are tuned to consumer web applications and map poorly onto tools, batch systems and internal services.

records.source: Design Council, Framework for Innovation (the Double Diamond)
records.population: UK design practice; framework originally launched 2004 and revised since
records.version_or_commit: current framework page as retrieved 2026-08-03; underlying model launched 2004
records.finding: Two diamonds, four stages of discover, define, develop and deliver, with the first diamond deciding what the right problem is and the second deciding what the right solution is. The single decision rule worth extracting is that divergence and convergence must be separated in time and named explicitly, because a team that converges while still diverging picks the first idea and calls it a decision. The framework is explicitly non-linear and expects loops back.
records.applicability_limits: It is a shape for talking about process, not a method, and it carries no criteria for when a diamond is finished. Nothing in the framework tells you how wide to diverge or how to compare options, so on its own it cannot resolve a prioritisation dispute. Widely taught, so teams often assume shared meaning where none exists.
records.review: on-change-of:a Design Council revision of the framework

records.source: Salgado Neto, Araujo and de Souza Santos, Collaborative and AI-Supported Requirements Elicitation: An Empirical Study
records.study_design: Controlled experiment across four conditions: collaborative elicitation without AI, collaboration with an in-platform LLM writer, direct LLM generation of requirements, and LLM synthesis of a human collaborative discussion transcript. Artefacts scored against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 quality criteria plus participant perception measures
records.population: Study participants performing an elicitation task on the Strateegia platform
records.model: GPT-family model via the platform's Writer applet, exact version not stated in the abstract
records.finding: The winning condition was neither humans alone nor the model alone. Human collaborative discussion followed by LLM synthesis of the transcript produced the highest-rated requirement artefacts and was perceived as clearer and easier to act on than unaided collaboration. The extractable rule is to keep humans generating the raw material and give the model the structuring job, rather than asking a model to originate requirements it has no access to the context for.
records.applicability_limits: Preprint, not yet peer-reviewed at time of access. Single platform, single task, participants rather than real stakeholders with real stakes, and the quality measure is conformance to a documentation standard rather than whether the resulting product succeeded. Conformance to 29148 is a proxy that rewards well-formed prose and cannot detect a well-written requirement for the wrong thing.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0413 shows that when the human input is itself simulated, the pipeline degrades sharply, which bounds how far the synthesis result can be pushed.
records.review: on-change-of:peer-reviewed publication of this study or a replication

records.source: Chen, Zhu and Zheng, When Synthetic Users Fail: A Cross-Domain Benchmark of LLM-Simulated Human Survey Responses
records.study_design: Benchmark against two real human survey datasets, the General Social Survey and the World Values Survey, comparing four LLMs across two model families against non-LLM statistical baselines at individual and segment level
records.population: US general social attitudes and cross-cultural values respondents
records.model: Four models spanning two families, from roughly 8B parameters to frontier scale
records.benchmark: General Social Survey and World Values Survey response prediction
records.licence: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence 1.0. Paraphrase only
records.finding: At the individual level no tested model beat even the strongest non-LLM baseline, and the models systematically over-determine demographics, treating identity as far more predictive of attitude than it is in real populations. On the segment-targeting task, which is exactly what a product team would use synthetic users for, models inflated between-segment gaps by two to four times and would have pointed a team at the wrong segment in half of the US cases and most of the cross-cultural ones. The rule is that synthetic respondents are not a cheap substitute for recruitment and are most wrong on the question teams most want to ask them.
records.applicability_limits: Attitudinal survey response prediction, not open-ended interview simulation, task performance or usability observation. A synthetic persona used to rehearse an interview guide or to generate candidate questions is not what this benchmark tests. Model capability moves quickly, so the specific failure margins are a snapshot and the direction of the finding is the durable part.
records.counter_evidence: Some 2026 work reports that synthetic respondents recover the direction and rough magnitude of aggregate attitudinal trends, which is consistent with this paper's finding that aggregate direction survives while individual and segment resolution does not.

records.source: Rosa, Moreno-Lumbreras, Robles and Gonzalez-Barahona, Understanding Specification-Driven Code Generation with LLMs: An Empirical Study Design
records.study_design: Stage 1 registered report, protocol and analysis plan peer-reviewed and accepted at SANER 2026 with continuity acceptance. Results not yet collected
records.population: Participants solving LiveCodeBench problems through a three-stage specification, tests, function workflow in a VS Code extension
records.finding: The state of the evidence is the finding. As of the cutoff, the question of whether human refinement of specifications and tests actually improves LLM-generated code has an accepted protocol and no results. Anyone asserting that spec-driven development measurably improves outcomes is asserting ahead of the evidence. The pre-registered structure, specification then tests then function, is itself worth noting as the shape the research community judged worth testing.
records.applicability_limits: Competitive-programming-style problems with closed, checkable specifications, which is the easiest possible case for spec-driven generation and the least like product discovery. Results, when they land, will not transfer to specifying a product whose acceptance criteria are contested.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0074 and EV-0075 present spec-driven development as an established improvement; this registered report shows the controlled evidence for that claim did not exist at the cutoff.

records.source: Teresa Torres, Product Talk, Opportunity Solution Trees
records.population: Product trios in product-led software companies coached by the author
records.version_or_commit: published 2023-12-06 in current form, updated May 2026, retrieved 2026-08-03
records.licence: Copyright Product Talk, all rights reserved. Paraphrase only
records.finding: A tree with a single business outcome at the root, customer opportunities below it, candidate solutions below those, and assumption tests at the leaves. Three rules do the work: opportunities are admitted only when grounded in a story from an actual interview rather than invented internally, effort is deliberately excluded when comparing opportunities so that cheapness cannot masquerade as value, and at least three candidate solutions are carried per opportunity so the first idea is never compared only against nothing.
records.applicability_limits: Explicitly scoped to a product trio working a single outcome, and the author states it is not a company strategy tool. It assumes weekly access to real customers, which pre-launch ventures do not have. Evidence is coaching practice, not controlled study, so the specific numbers, three to four interviews per revision and three solutions per opportunity, are conventions rather than findings and should be treated as such.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0405 implies that where experimentation is cheap, carrying three candidate solutions through analysis is more expensive than testing all three.
records.review: on-change-of:a substantive revision of the Product Talk opportunity solution tree article

records.source: Marty Cagan, SVPG, The Four Big Risks
records.population: Product organisations advised by SVPG, mostly funded technology companies with dedicated product, design and engineering roles
records.licence: Copyright Silicon Valley Product Group. Paraphrase only
records.finding: Four risks are named and each is assigned an owner: value, whether anyone will choose it, owned by product; usability, whether they can work it out, owned by design; feasibility, whether it can be built with what is available, owned by engineering; and viability, whether it works for the business including go-to-market and monetisation, owned by product. The useful move is that discovery is defined as retiring these risks before delivery, which converts the vague question of whether discovery is done into four separately answerable questions.
records.applicability_limits: The ownership split presumes three distinct people. In a solo or agent-driven venture one operator holds all four, and the most likely failure is that the two risks the operator finds interesting get tested while the other two are assumed away. No empirical validation is offered; the four categories are an organising heuristic that has become widespread through repetition rather than through measurement.

records.source: Sean McBride, Intercom, RICE: Simple prioritization for product managers
records.population: Intercom's own product team, one company, one period
records.finding: Score equals reach times impact times confidence, divided by effort, where reach is people or events per fixed period, impact is a coarse multiplier from 0.25 to 3, confidence is a percentage tier of 100, 80 or 50 with anything below 50 declared a moonshot, and effort is person-months. The genuinely useful element is the explicit confidence multiplier, because it forces a team to write down how much of the score is guesswork, and the article states plainly that the score is not a rule and dependencies may reorder it.
records.applicability_limits: One company's internal tool published as a blog post, with no evaluation of whether RICE-ranked backlogs outperformed any alternative. The multiplication of three subjective estimates produces a precise-looking number whose error bars are never shown, and the coarse impact scale means a single step changes the score by a factor of two. It cannot price options that are cheap to test but high variance, which is exactly what EV-0405 says most ideas are.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0405 shows expert estimates of impact are close to uninformative at the idea level, which undercuts the impact term that RICE depends on most.

records.source: Strategyn, What is Outcome-Driven Innovation, Anthony Ulwick
records.study_design: Survey-based method: importance and satisfaction rated 1 to 10 on desired outcome statements, typically 180 to 600 respondents, combined by the opportunity algorithm
records.population: Client engagements of a consultancy that owns the method
records.version_or_commit: vendor pages as retrieved 2026-08-03; method dates from the 1990s, opportunity algorithm published 2002
records.licence: Copyright Strategyn; Outcome-Driven Innovation is a registered trade mark. Paraphrase only
records.finding: The method's real contribution is the unit of analysis: a desired outcome written as a measurable statement of a job step, which is stable across solutions in a way that feature requests are not. The opportunity score, importance plus the positive part of importance minus satisfaction, then ranks outcomes on the claim that opportunity lives where importance is high and satisfaction is low. The transferable rule is to elicit outcomes rather than features, because outcomes survive a change of technology and features do not.
records.applicability_limits: The scoring arithmetic is contested: adding an importance rating to a difference of two subjective ratings on the same scale has no clear justification, and the method's owner has said publicly that exact ordering is not the point. Everything published about effectiveness comes from the consultancy that sells the method, with no independent controlled evaluation located at the cutoff. Sample sizes of 180 to 600 are out of reach for an early venture, which means the outcome-elicitation half transfers and the scoring half does not.
records.counter_evidence: Independent practitioner critiques question the subtraction of satisfaction from importance; no controlled study either supporting or refuting the algorithm was located.
records.review: on-change-of:publication of an independent controlled evaluation of ODI

records.source: Mike Cohn, Mountain Goat Software, Are 64% of Features Really Rarely or Never Used?
records.study_design: Provenance investigation of a widely cited statistic
records.population: The original Standish Group data behind the claim
records.version_or_commit: article as retrieved 2026-08-03; the claim it examines dates from a Jim Johnson keynote at XP 2002
records.licence: Copyright Mountain Goat Software. Paraphrase only
records.finding: The statistic that 64 per cent of features are rarely or never used, and its sibling that 45 per cent are never used, traces back to a conference keynote reporting on four internal applications. It has been repeated for over two decades by people who did not check the base. The rule this establishes is procedural rather than substantive: a number that justifies a discovery process must have its own provenance recorded, or the process is being sold on evidence that does not exist.
records.applicability_limits: A provenance critique, not a replacement measurement. It does not establish that feature underuse is rare, and independent instrumented data such as EV-0420 points the same way with a far larger base. Debunking the number does not debunk the underlying concern.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0420 reports a similar magnitude from instrumented telemetry across many products, so the direction of the original claim survives even though its cited evidence does not.
records.review: on-change-of:publication of a peer-reviewed measurement of feature usage distribution

records.source: Pendo, 2019 Feature Adoption Report
records.study_design: Observational telemetry analysis of in-product click and feature-usage events across the vendor's installed base
records.population: Software products instrumented with Pendo, skewed towards B2B SaaS applications that buy product analytics
records.version_or_commit: 2019 edition, retrieved 2026-08-03; no later edition located at the cutoff
records.finding: Usage is extremely concentrated. The report puts roughly 80 per cent of features in the average product as rarely or never used, with click volume concentrating in a small minority of the feature set, and it finds that the best products concentrate usage across a noticeably wider share of features than the average product does. The decision rule is that the default outcome of shipping a feature is that almost nobody touches it, so the burden of proof sits with building, not with investigating.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor research with a commercial interest in the conclusion that unused features are a problem their tool solves, no published methodology for how a feature is delimited or what counts as used, and a sample confined to companies that bought product analytics. Seven years old at the cutoff and not refreshed. Treat the magnitude as indicative and the direction as well supported.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0419 shows how easily a number of exactly this shape becomes folklore; this one should be cited with its vendor status attached every time.
records.review: on-change-of:a newer Pendo feature adoption report or an independent telemetry study

records.source: PagerDuty Incident Response documentation, severity levels
records.finding: Severity is a decision made under uncertainty, so the ladder carries a tie-break rule rather than a definition alone: five SEV levels ordered so that lower numbers are more urgent, an explicit instruction to assume the higher level when unsure, and a ban on litigating the level during the incident with the argument deferred to the postmortem. One threshold is mechanical rather than advisory: SEV-2 and above switches the organisation into major incident response, so the label is a mode selector and not a report field.
records.applicability_limits: Written for a company with a staffed on-call rota and a distinct incident commander role; the five levels assume enough volume that SEV-4 and SEV-5 are worth separating. A one-person venture gains the tie-break rule and the mode threshold, not the five rungs. Says nothing about non-outage support items such as billing questions or feature requests.
records.counter_evidence: The ladder is stated as PagerDuty practice with no measured outcome; no evidence is offered that five levels beat three, and EV-0211 shows that the duration measures usually attached to severity bands are analysed badly in the industry.

records.source: PagerDuty Business Incident Response documentation, recognising and declaring a business incident
records.version_or_commit: site build of PagerDuty/business-response-docs inspected 2026-08-03; no version string published on the page
records.licence: Apache-2.0 (repository LICENSE for PagerDuty/business-response-docs); page itself shows no notice
records.finding: Customer-facing escalation is a separate decision from technical escalation and is scored, not felt: the guidance names three factors, visibility (core service or an ancillary one), actual rather than potential impact at the current traffic level, and duration so far plus confidence of resolution within the hour, and tells the organisation to write a formula combining them. The declaration itself is a deliberate manual page to a named business stakeholder, not an automatic consequence of a monitoring threshold, and a business subject matter expert joins the technical call as the person who decides whether the business responds.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes a senior leadership bench to page and a technical incident already running underneath. In a small venture the business stakeholder and the incident commander are the same person, so the value is the three-factor score and the written formula, not the role split. Gives no template for the customer message itself.
records.counter_evidence: No outcome data. The advice to keep declaration manual conflicts with the common practice of auto-declaring on an SLO burn alert, and neither position is evidenced here.

records.source: Google SRE Book, chapter 14, Managing Incidents
records.version_or_commit: web edition of the 2016 book, copyright 2017 Google Inc, page inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (paraphrase only, no verbatim reuse, no derivatives)
records.finding: Communication is a named role held by someone who is not fixing the system, sitting alongside incident command, operations and planning, and only the operations role touches the system. Declaration is driven by three objective triggers rather than judgement: a second team is needed, the problem is customer-visible, or an hour of focused work has not resolved it. The shared artefact is a live state document that several people edit concurrently, which is what later becomes the postmortem input, and handover of command is an explicit spoken transfer with acknowledgement.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes at least three or four available responders. The one-hour trigger is calibrated to Google-scale services and is not evidence for any particular threshold elsewhere. Licence forbids copying the role definitions verbatim into a pack, so only the principle transfers.
records.counter_evidence: The role separation is Google practice with no comparative measurement. EV-0200 places the postmortem on a fixed clock, which is complementary, but neither source shows that separating the communications role improves customer outcomes rather than internal focus.

records.source: Kubernetes contributor guide, issue triage
records.finding: Triage is a labelling contract on orthogonal axes rather than a single queue position: kind (what sort of thing it is), priority (five bands from critical-urgent through awaiting-more-evidence), owning group, and a separate triage/accepted flag so that untriaged is a visible machine-queryable state rather than an absence. Two rules make the queue finite: support questions are labelled and routed out of the bug tracker rather than answered in it, and items lacking reproduction or information are closed on a timer, with a ninety-day inactivity clock adding a stale label and a twenty-day silence closing unreproducible reports. A priority band exists specifically for items that are plausible but not yet supported by evidence, which keeps opinion out of the backlog.
records.applicability_limits: Designed for a public volunteer-staffed tracker where the reporter is not a paying customer and where closing a stale issue costs nothing contractual. Applying the auto-close timer to a paying customer's complaint is a different act, see EV-0425. The five priority bands assume many owners; a solo venture needs the axes, not the bands.
records.counter_evidence: The stale bot is contested inside the project itself, with maintainers filing that it closes important bugs. EV-0425 requires a complaint to be resolved and responded to rather than timed out, which is a direct conflict of obligation.

records.source: ISO 10002:2018, Quality management, Customer satisfaction, Guidelines for complaints handling in organizations
records.version_or_commit: third edition, ISO 10002:2018, confirmed current at 2026-08-03
records.licence: ISO copyright, paywalled; paraphrase only, no reuse of text
records.finding: A complaint is a closed loop with named accountability at every hop, not a ticket that ages out: the route to complain must itself be visible and free to use, receipt is acknowledged, the complainant is told the outcome, and the loop is only closed when the complainant has been responded to. The second obligation is the one that makes support a product function: complaint data must be analysed in aggregate and fed into improvement of the product and the process, so recording without periodic synthesis is a failure of the standard rather than a missed nicety. Fairness and objectivity are treated as design properties of the process, which in practice means the resolution rule is written before the complaint arrives.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance, not certifiable requirements, and written for organisations large enough to have a quality management system and trained personnel. Says nothing about response time targets, channels or tooling, and nothing about digital products specifically. Paywalled, so the pack can only carry the principle.
records.counter_evidence: Directly conflicts with the stale-and-close discipline in EV-0424. No evidence is offered that the closed-loop process improves retention or satisfaction; the standard is consensus practice.

records.source: ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018, Information technology, Service management, Part 1: Service management system requirements
records.version_or_commit: third edition, ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018, confirmed current at 2026-08-03
records.finding: The 2018 edition splits what earlier editions merged: incident management and service request fulfilment become separate sets of requirements, because the target differs. An incident is an unplanned interruption whose goal is to restore service, and a service request is a routine ask whose goal is to fulfil it, so measuring them in one queue with one target hides both. Classification and prioritisation are ordered steps, classification first, and the standard also requires a defined route for escalation and for major incidents to be handled under a separate declared procedure.
records.applicability_limits: Requirements for a certifiable management system, aimed at service providers with contractual obligations. The documentation burden is disproportionate below a few staff. The load-bearing transferable part is the two-queue split and the ordering of classify before prioritise, not the management-system apparatus.
records.counter_evidence: No outcome evidence that the split improves service; the standard is consensus. Practitioner tooling frequently collapses both into one ticket type without reported harm.

records.source: Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review
records.study_design: Cross-sectional correlation of survey responses against firm growth rates, industry by industry; instrument selection by comparing candidate questions
records.population: Customers of firms across roughly a dozen US industries, Bain and Satmetrix data
records.version_or_commit: December 2003 issue article, as published; inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Harvard Business Publishing copyright, paywalled; paraphrase only
records.finding: The claim under test in every later argument about support measurement: that a single likelihood-to-recommend question, scored as promoters minus detractors, correlates with firm growth better than longer satisfaction instruments, and that its practical virtue is that one number can be acted on by front-line staff without interpretation. The operational idea worth keeping independent of the statistics is that a measurement nobody can act on the same week is not a support metric.
records.applicability_limits: The original analysis is industry-level and cross-sectional, from a consultancy selling the method, and covers consumer industries in one country in the early 2000s. It says nothing about the sample size at which the score is stable, which is the binding constraint for a venture with tens of customers.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0428 attempted replication and failed to reproduce the superiority claim, which is the load-bearing disagreement in this pack.
records.review: on-change-of:a further independent replication of the net promoter superiority claim

records.source: Keiningham, Cooil, Andreassen and Aksoy, A Longitudinal Examination of Net Promoter and Firm Revenue Growth, Journal of Marketing
records.study_design: Longitudinal replication attempt using an independent national satisfaction panel, comparing explanatory power of net promoter against the American Customer Satisfaction Index on the industries cited as exemplars in the original claim
records.population: 21 firms and more than 15,500 interviews from the Norwegian Customer Satisfaction Barometer
records.version_or_commit: Journal of Marketing, volume 71, issue 3, July 2007, pages 39 to 51
records.licence: American Marketing Association and SAGE copyright, paywalled; paraphrase only
records.finding: The superiority claim does not replicate. Using the very industries named as exemplars, explanatory power for the recommendation-based score and for a conventional satisfaction index was statistically indistinguishable, so choosing the single-question instrument buys operational simplicity and not predictive accuracy. The decision rule that follows is to treat any loyalty instrument as a trend line about the same population over time, never as a benchmark against other firms and never as evidence that one instrument sees something another cannot.
records.applicability_limits: One country, one panel, twenty-one firms, and the period studied predates subscription software. It refutes a superiority claim rather than showing the score is useless, and it does not address small-sample behaviour, which is the failure mode that actually bites a venture with fifty customers.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0427 is the claim it contradicts, and the method retains very wide industry adoption regardless, which is itself weak evidence that practitioners find the operational simplicity worth the loss of rigour.

records.source: Dixon, Freeman and Toman, Stop Trying to Delight Your Customers, Harvard Business Review
records.study_design: Cross-sectional survey of service interactions with self-reported loyalty intent, plus interviews with service leaders; run by a commercial research membership
records.population: Approximately 97,000 customers of hundreds of organisations reporting on service interactions, plus several hundred service organisations
records.version_or_commit: July to August 2010 issue article, as published; inspected 2026-08-03
records.licence: Harvard Business Publishing copyright, paywalled; paraphrase only
records.finding: Exceeding expectations in a service interaction did not separate loyal from disloyal customers, while the effort the customer had to spend did, with high-effort interactions overwhelmingly associated with reported disloyalty. The mechanical driver named is channel switching: a large share of people who telephone have already failed on the website, so a self-service channel that does not resolve the question converts into an assisted contact with the customer's effort already spent. The decision rule is that self-service is only a deflection when it resolves; an unresolving self-service layer adds a hop rather than removing one.
records.applicability_limits: Cross-sectional and self-reported, measuring stated loyalty intent rather than observed retention, and run by a vendor selling the resulting effort metric. English-language contact-centre settings. The headline proportions have not been independently replicated at the same magnitude, although the direction of the effort effect is widely reproduced.
records.counter_evidence: EV-0432 argues the opposite posture for early-stage ventures, that founders should take extraordinary and unscalable measures to delight small numbers of users. The two are not reconciled by evidence, only by scale.
records.review: on-change-of:an independent replication of the effort and loyalty association

records.source: Kingman, The single server queue in heavy traffic, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
records.study_design: Analytical derivation, heavy-traffic diffusion approximation for the general single-server queue; not an empirical study
records.licence: Cambridge University Press copyright, paywalled; the result itself is mathematics and not subject to reuse restriction
records.finding: Waiting time in a single-server queue is the product of three factors, a utilisation term that behaves as rho over one minus rho, a variability term averaging the squared coefficients of variation of arrivals and of service, and the mean service time. The consequence for a founder who is the only support agent is not gradual: at seventy per cent utilisation the expected wait is roughly two and a third service times, at eighty-five per cent roughly five and two thirds, at ninety-five per cent nineteen. Response time therefore degrades non-linearly before any visible capacity problem, and the two levers that work are reducing variability and holding deliberate slack, not working faster.
records.applicability_limits: A heavy-traffic approximation, most accurate near saturation and less so at low load. Assumes one server, first come first served, no priority classes and no abandonment, so a severity-prioritised desk behaves differently in detail while keeping the same qualitative blow-up. It gives no target utilisation; that is a policy choice.
records.counter_evidence: None on the mathematics. The practical caveat is that real support queues have priority classes, batching and customers who give up, all of which the single-server model omits.

records.source: Braun and Clarke, Using thematic analysis in psychology, Qualitative Research in Psychology
records.study_design: Methodological paper specifying a six-phase analytic procedure and the decisions that must be declared for it to be auditable
records.version_or_commit: volume 3, issue 2, 2006, pages 77 to 101; the authors' later revisions restate phase two as generating rather than searching for themes
records.licence: Taylor and Francis copyright, paywalled; author-hosted copies exist; paraphrase only
records.finding: Themes are constructed by the analyst, not discovered lying in the data, and the authors treat the phrase that a theme emerged as a claim that hides the decisions that produced it. The transferable discipline for turning a support inbox into backlog items is that four choices are declared before coding rather than after: whether coding is inductive or driven by an existing frame, whether it reads the surface or the underlying meaning, what counts as a theme, and what the whole data set is. Prevalence is then reported against a stated denominator, because a count of tickets mentioning a thing is meaningless without the population it was drawn from.
records.applicability_limits: Written for qualitative research in psychology, not for support triage, and it offers no threshold for how many tickets make a theme actionable.
